title: The Hymn of the Vast Grace-Light

intro.title: Introduction: Thiru Arutpa
paras: Thiru Arutpa, which means Divine Songs of Grace, is a collection of poems written by Ramalinga Adigal, lovingly known as Vallalar.

The entire poetic work is divided into 6 volumes or Thirumurais. The poems narrate the spiritual journey of Vallalar. From his early days of worship into the Saiva Siddhanta doctrine, the suffering from separation from the divine, to the final realization of the Arut Perun Jothi (Vast Grace Light) in his late stage of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Sangam philosophy and way of life. The core philosophical pillars of the Thiru Arutpa include:
Active Compassion: The foundation is Jeeva Karunyam, or active compassion for all living beings as basis to spiritual life
Unity of All Beings: The Arutpa teaches Anma Neya Orumaipadu, or the Unity of Souls, asserting that every creature shares the exact same spiritual essence.
Rejection of Division: Vallalar wholly rejected caste systems, religious divisions, and sectarian hierarchies.
The Divine Light: The ultimate recognition is that Arutperunjothi, the supreme divine light, dwells within every single soul without exception.
Ultimately, the Thiru Arutpa is a spiritual guide toward boundless compassion to all life, self-realization, and what Vallalar taught as the physical body's ability to reach a deathless state.

intro.title: Introduction: Thiru Arutpa Sixth Thirumurai
paras: The Thiru Arutpa is the collected poetry of Ramalinga Adigal, and it is arranged in six parts called Thirumurai. This is the sixth and last.

The first five volumes were written by a younger Ramalinga inside a tradition. They are temple hymns. They name places, they address deities by their local names, and they follow forms Tamil devotional poetry had used for a thousand years. They are beautiful, and they are recognisable.

The Sixth is what came after. These are the works of his final years, written at Vadalur and at Mettukuppam, in the same period when he opened a kitchen that fed anyone who came and built a hall with no god in it. Four things change.

He names the path. In the earlier volumes he is a devotee. Here he is teaching something, and it has a name: Suddha Sanmarkkam, the pure true path. He describes it, he sets out what it asks, and he tells people to enter it.

He says caste, creed and sect are false. Not incomplete. False. He uses the word poy, a lie, and he says he was told so from the beginning. The man writing the Sixth Thirumurai has stopped working within the religions and has begun speaking past them.

He says the body does not have to die. The teaching on deathlessness, on the body remade by grace, appears here and nowhere earlier. It is the hardest part of his work and the part most often argued over.

He puts compassion at the gate. Jeeva Karunyam, mercy toward every living thing, is not presented as one virtue among many. It is the condition. Without it, he says, nothing else opens. This is why the free kitchen and these poems belong to the same act.
The form changes too. The temple hymn gives way to direct address. He is no longer singing about the divine from a shrine. He is speaking to it, and reporting what it said back.

A note on the arrangement. Ramalinga did not publish these works himself. He wrote as occasion demanded and left the ordering to others. His disciple Thozhuvur Velayutha Mudaliar, who had edited the earlier volumes during his lifetime, gathered the late writings after 1874 and arranged them. The six-part division is the work of the disciples, not of Ramalinga. Later editors, chiefly Ooran Adigal, reordered the volumes by date of composition, which is why some poems sit in different Thirumurai in different editions.

A note on this volume. The Sixth Thirumurai is published in two books. The first contains the Arutperunjothi Agaval alone, which at 1,596 lines is a book in itself. The second contains everything else. Both are free.

intro.title: Introduction: The Hymn of the Vast Grace-light
paras: The Arutperunjothi Agaval, the Hymn of the Vast Grace-Light, is the greatest work of Ramalinga Adigal, the Tamil saint lovingly known as Vallalar. He wrote it in his last and most mature years, at Mettukuppam in south India. It is said that he wrote it in one unbroken session, in a single night.

It has 1,596 lines. Its subject is the Arutperunjothi, the Vast Grace Light. The poem describes what that Light is, how everything that exists came out of it and is still held by it, and what happens inside a person when it is let in.

It begins by naming it. For 437 couplets, every second line ends in the same word. Then the naming stops, and the poem calls the same thing mother, father, friend, medicine, gold, mountain, ocean, lamp. At the end the first name returns, and the poem closes on the line it opened with.
Three things are said clearly. Caste, creed and sect are false. The path of non-violence is the path of grace. Every living thing is to be seen as your own.
More than a century later, devotees all over the world still wake up before dawn to sing these blissful lines.

works.title: The Hymn of the Vast Grace-light

translit: aruṭperuñ jōti yaruṭperuñ jōti aruṭperuñ jōti yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Vast Grace-Light, Vast Grace-Light. Vast Grace-Light, Vast Grace-Light
commentary: The poem begins as a powerful chant, repeating the name of the divine reality: Arut Perum Jothi (Vast Grace-Light) four times. This repetition is more than for emphasis; it is a spiritual practice, a way to focus the mind and invoke the presence of the divine light. The 4 times repetition may indicate the presence of the Vast grace light in all the 4 planes :
• Agam - Interior / Deep Interior
• Agappuram - Interior-Exterior / Inner-Outer
• Puram - Exterior / Outer
• Purappuram - Exterior-Exterior / Outermost-Outer

translit: aruṭciva neṟicā raruṭperu nilaivāḻ aruṭciva patiyā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the essence of the path of Grace-Siva, the life of the state of vast grace, the Lord of Grace-Siva.
commentary: The Divine Light is presented as both the path and the destination. It is the very essence of the way of Grace-Siva (Arutciva neṟi), the life force within the ultimate state of grace, and the supreme Lord who presides over it.

translit: ākama muṭimēl āraṇa muṭimēl ākaniṉ ṟōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which stands and soars as the very substance above the crown of the Agamas and the crown of the Vedas
commentary: This light is the ultimate reality, surpassing even the most revered scriptures. It stands above both the Vedas (ancient hymns and philosophy) and the Agamas (texts on temple worship and doctrine), signifying that direct experience of the Grace-Light is a higher truth than any scripture.

translit: ikanilaip poruḷāyp paranilaip poruḷāy akamaṟap poruntiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the substance of this earthly state and the substance of the transcendent state, perfectly united so the ego dissolves.
commentary: The Grace-Light is not a remote, otherworldly power; it is the fundamental substance of both our physical world and the highest spiritual realm. Experiencing this perfect unity of the worldly and the transcendent dissolves the ego, the sense of a separate 'I'.

translit: īṉamiṉ ṟikaparat tiraṇṭiṉmēṟ poruḷāy āṉaliṉ ṟōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the flawless substance above both this world and the next, soaring without limit.
commentary: While the Grace-Light constitutes both this world and the transcendent one, it is not limited by them. It is a reality that exists beyond and above all realms, perfect and boundless in its nature.

translit: uraimaṉaṅ kaṭanta voruperu veḷimēl araicucey tōṅku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, reigning supreme over the one great expanse beyond speech and mind.
commentary: The divine reality, Arutperunjothi (Vast Grace-Light), operates from a realm that cannot be grasped by the intellect or described with words. It is a state of pure being, a great expanse that is fundamentally beyond the limits of human experience.

translit: ūkkamu muṇarcciyu moḷitaru mākkaiyum ākkamu maruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously bestowed zeal, consciousness, a body radiating light, and prosperity.
commentary: All the gifts of life, both internal and external, come from this one divine source. Arutperunjothi bestows spiritual qualities like zeal and consciousness and physical ones like a luminous body and material abundance.

translit: ellaiyil piṟappeṉu miruṅkaṭal kaṭattiyeṉ allalai nīkkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which made me cross the vast ocean of boundless birth and removed my suffering.
commentary: Liberation from the painful cycle of repeated birth and death is a central goal in many Indian traditions. Vallalar identifies Arutperunjothi as the sole power that can carry a soul across this "ocean of birth" and end all suffering.

translit: ēṟā nilaimicai yēṟṟiyeṉ ṟaṉakkē āṟāṟu kāṭṭiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which raised me to the unascendable state and, for me alone, revealed the thirty-six principles.
commentary: The Light of Grace can lift a person to a level of spiritual realization that is otherwise impossible to attain through personal effort. This grace also reveals deep truths about existence, represented here by the "thirty-six principles" (tattvas), a traditional map of all the elements that make up the cosmos and the individual.

translit: aiyamun tiripu maṟutteṉa tuṭampiṉuḷ aiyamu nīkkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which severed doubt and delusion, and also removed the phlegm within my body.
commentary: The spiritual and the physical are joined here. Divine grace purifies everything at once, clearing mental obstacles like doubt while also healing the physical body, represented here by removing "phlegm" (aiyam or kapham), a cause of illness in traditional siddha medicine.

translit: oṉṟeṉa viraṇṭeṉa voṉṟiraṇ ṭeṉavivai yaṉṟeṉa viḷaṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, shining as that which is not one, not two, nor one-and-two.
commentary: The Great Light of Grace, Arutperunjothi, cannot be confined by philosophical definitions. It is not "one" (non-dualism), "two" (dualism), or a mixture of both. These are just mental concepts, and the ultimate reality transcends them all, inviting direct experience (anubhavam) over intellectual debate.

translit: ōtā tuṇarntiṭa voḷiyaḷit teṉakkē ātāra mākiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which gave me light to realize it without study, and which became my foundation.
commentary: True spiritual knowledge does not come from books or intellectual learning. Vallalar says it is a direct gift of Grace, an inner light that allows one to understand without being taught. This Grace becomes the very ground of one's being, a foundation more solid than any external authority.

translit: auviya mātiyō rāṟun tavirttapēr avviyal vaḻuttu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, whose nature is acclaimed by the great ones who have relinquished the six vices beginning with envy.
commentary: The great ones who have overcome the six inner enemies, lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy, praise the nature of the Divine Light. Purification of the mind and heart is what makes true praise possible.

translit: tirunilait taṉiveḷi civaveḷi yeṉumōr aruḷveḷip pativaḷa raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, flourishing in the domain of the space of Grace, a singular expanse known as the unique space of the sacred state and the space of Siva.
commentary: The Great Light of Grace is found in a "space" that is not physical. This is the pure, open expanse of consciousness itself, which Vallalar calls the space of Grace, the sacred state, and the space of Siva (the ultimate reality). It is the boundless inner realm where the divine resides.

translit: cuttacaṉ mārkka cukattaṉi veḷiyeṉum attakaic ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is the Chit Sabhai of such a nature, known as the unique space of the bliss of Suddha Sanmarkkam.
commentary: This inner expanse of consciousness is the true temple, the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness). It is not a physical place but the center of our own being. To experience this inner space is the unique bliss of Suddha Sanmarkkam, the True Path of Purity that Vallalar teaches.

translit: cuttameyñ ñāṉa cukōtaya veḷiyeṉu attu vitaccapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the hall of non-duality, which is the space where pure, true wisdom blissfully arises.
commentary: The Divine Light reveals itself in the 'hall of non-duality' (attuvita sabai). This is a state of consciousness where the feeling of separation between the self and God dissolves into a blissful, unified wisdom.

translit: tūyaka lānta cukantaru veḷiyeṉum āyaciṟ capaiyi laruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the precious hall of consciousness, which is the space that gives the bliss of pure Kalāntam.
commentary: The Light resides in the inner 'hall of consciousness' (chitsabai), bringing a bliss that comes from reaching Kalāntam. This is a state that transcends all the structures and building blocks of the material and subtle cosmos, a reality beyond everything that has been created.

translit: ñāṉayō kānta naṭattiru veḷiyeṉum āṉiyil ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the flawless hall of consciousness, which is the sacred space of the dance at the culmination of the yoga of wisdom.
commentary: The practice of ñāṇa yōkam, the yoga of wisdom, culminates in reaching a sacred inner space. Here, one witnesses a divine 'dance' which is the dynamic, vibrant play of the Divine Light itself within one's own flawless consciousness.

translit: vimalapō tāntamā meypporuḷ veḷiyeṉum amalaciṟ capaiyi laruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the immaculate hall of consciousness, which is the space of the true substance at the culmination of pure knowing.
commentary: When the mind is purified, one arrives at a state of 'pure knowing' (vimala pōtam). In this immaculate inner space, the Divine Light is perceived directly as the meypporuḷ, the one 'true substance' and fundamental reality of all existence.

translit: periyanā tāntap perunilai veḷiyeṉum ariyaciṟ ṟampalat taruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the precious Chitrambalam, which is the space of the great state of Nādāntam.
commentary: The Divine Light is found in the Chitrambalam, the 'small sacred hall', which represents the innermost sanctum of the self. Reaching this space is to attain Nādāntam, a state of profound stillness that exists beyond even the primordial sound from which the universe arises.

translit: cuttavē tāntat turiyamēl veḷiyeṉum attaku ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of that distinguished Chit Sabhai, which is the space beyond the Turiya state of pure Vedanta.
commentary: The ancient philosophy of Vedanta describes four states of consciousness, with the highest transcendent state being turīya. Vallalar says the experience of Arutperunjothi happens in a space even beyond that. He points to an experience of God that surpasses the highest concepts of traditional philosophy.

translit: cuttacit tānta cukapperu veḷiyeṉum attaṉic ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of that unique Chit Sabhai, which is the great space of bliss of pure Siddhanta.
commentary: After referencing Vedanta, Vallalar now turns to another major philosophical tradition, Siddhanta. He identifies the "hall of consciousness" (cit-sabai) with the ultimate goal of Siddhanta practice: an infinite, great space of pure bliss. In doing so, he shows how the experience of the Divine Light fulfills the highest aspirations of different spiritual paths.

translit: takarameyñ ñāṉat taṉipperu veḷiyeṉum akara nilaippati yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the primal abode, the state of 'A', which is the unique great space of true wisdom of the Takaram.
commentary: The search for God often looks outward, but here the divine is located deep within. It is found in the takaram, a subtle space within the heart known to yogis. This inner space is the source of all things, symbolized by 'A' (akara nilai), the first letter and primal sound. This is the place of true wisdom.

translit: tattuvā tīta taṉipporuḷ veḷiyeṉum attiru vampalat taruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the sacred Ambalam, which is the space of the unique substance transcending the tattvas.
commentary: Indian philosophy maps the universe through a system of tattvas, the fundamental building blocks of all cosmic and psychological reality. Vallalar says Arutperunjothi is found in a sacred "divine hall" (ampalam) that is beyond all of these principles. The reality of the Light transcends the entire structure of the created world.

translit: caccitā ṉantat taṉippara veḷiyeṉum acciya lampalat taruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the Ambalam of that true nature, which is the unique supreme space of Satchidananda.
commentary: Vallalar now connects the Divine Light to the ultimate description of God in Vedanta philosophy: saccidānanda, which means Being-Consciousness-Bliss. The "divine hall" (ampalam) where the Light shines is the living experience of absolute existence, perfect awareness, and infinite joy, all as one reality.

translit: cākāk kalainilai taḻaittiṭu veḷiyeṉum ākā yattoḷi raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which shines in the ākāyam, the space where the art of deathlessness thrives.
commentary: The 'art of deathlessness' is achieved within a subtle space called ākāyam (ether). This is a transcendent field of consciousness where the Grace-Light shines, making eternal life possible.

translit: kāraṇa kāriyaṅ kāṭṭiṭu veḷiyeṉum āraṇac ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the Hall of Wisdom of the Āraṇam, the space that reveals cause and effect.
commentary: The Grace-Light illuminates the nature of reality, revealing the universal law of cause and effect. This light is the true Hall of Wisdom, the living truth that the ancient scriptures, the Āraṇam (Vedas), point towards.

translit: ēka maṉēka meṉappakar veḷiyeṉum ākamac ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the Hall of Wisdom of the Āgamam, the space proclaimed as both one and many.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the ultimate reality, which is simultaneously a single, unified source and the countless diverse things in creation. This truth, that the One becomes the Many, is a central teaching found in sacred texts known as the Āgamam.

translit: vētā kamaṅkaḷiṉ viḷaivukaṭ kellām ātāra māñcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the Hall that is the foundation for all the fruits of the Vedas and the Āgamams.
commentary: All the spiritual benefits, wisdom, and liberation promised by the great scriptures, the Vedas and Āgamams, have their source in this one reality. The Grace-Light is more than one path among many; it is the foundation and fulfillment of them all.

translit: eṉṟā tiyacuṭark kiyaṉilai yāyatu vaṉṟān tiruccapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the mighty Sacred Hall that is the inherent plane for the primordial luminaries.
commentary: The great lights of the cosmos, such as the sun, moon, and fire, are not self-sustaining. They all draw their existence and power from a deeper, more fundamental source: the Vast Grace-Light. It is the original light that gives light to all other lights.

translit: camayaṅ kaṭanta taṉipporuḷ veḷiyāy amaiyun tiruccapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the sacred assembly which is the space of the unique Reality, transcending all religions.
commentary: The Grace-Light, or Arutperunjothi, cannot be contained within any single religion. It is the one universal reality that transcends all different paths and belief systems. This is a core idea for Vallalar: the ultimate truth is available to everyone, regardless of their religious affiliation.

translit: muccuṭar kaḷumoḷi muyaṅkuṟa vaḷittaruḷ accuṭa rāñcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the assembly that is the Light Itself, which graciously makes the three luminaries unite their own light.
commentary: The three great lights of our world are the sun, the moon, and fire. Vallalar says that the Grace-Light is the ultimate source that enables these three to shine, and it is also the force that harmonizes them. The ultimate reality is a unifying power, bringing different forms of energy and light into a single, cohesive whole.

translit: turiyamuṅ kaṭanta cukapū raṇantarum ariyaciṟ ṟampalat taruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the rare Chitrambalam, granting the perfect bliss that transcends even Turiyam.
commentary: Traditional philosophy describes four states of consciousness: waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and a fourth, transcendent state called Turiyam. Vallalar says the experience of the Grace-Light, found in the Chitrambalam (the hall of pure consciousness), delivers a bliss that surpasses even this highest state. He is pointing to an experience that goes beyond all known categories of spiritual attainment.

translit: evvakaic cukaṅkaḷu miṉituṟa vaḷittaruḷ avvakaic ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the Chit Sabhai of such a nature, graciously and sweetly bestowing every kind of bliss.
commentary: The Chit Sabhai, or hall of consciousness, is the inner space where the Grace-Light reveals itself. Vallalar describes it as the source of every imaginable kind of bliss, given freely and sweetly. This is not a harsh or remote reality, but a source of profound and gentle joy.

translit: iyaṟkaiyuṇ maiyatā yiyaṟkaiyiṉ pamumām ayarppilāc ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the unfailing Chit Sabhai, which is natural Reality and natural Bliss.
commentary: Most people think of reality as something to be discovered and bliss as something to be earned. Vallalar says both are our natural state. The Grace-Light reveals that reality and bliss are not artificial or external, but are the very nature of existence itself, always present and unfailing.

translit: cākkirā tītat taṉiveḷi yāyniṟai vākkiya ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the Chit Sabhai, which fills and is the singular expanse beyond the waking state.
commentary: This hall of consciousness exists in a state beyond our normal waking awareness. This state, called jāgrat-atīta (beyond the waking state), is a singular, all-pervading expanse filled by the Divine Light.

translit: cuṭṭutaṟ karitāñ cukātīta veḷiyeṉum aṭṭamēṟ ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the Chit Sabhai on the high dais, which is the indefinable expanse beyond bliss.
commentary: The experience of this divine space is so profound it is called sukha-atīta, an expanse beyond even our highest concept of bliss. It is a reality that cannot be pointed to or described with ordinary language.

translit: navantavir nilaikaḷu naṇṇumōr nilaiyāy avantavir ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the Chit Sabhai that ends futility, itself the one state attained by transcending the nine states to be shed.
commentary: To reach this state of absolute reality, one must move past all lesser stages of being. The Chit Sabhai is the final destination beyond nine traditional states of consciousness, the one state where all spiritual striving and futility finally end.

translit: upayapak kaṅkaḷu moṉṟeṉak kāṭṭiya apayaciṟ capaiyi laruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the Chit Sabhai of refuge, which shows that opposing sides are one.
commentary: This divine space provides abhaya, or absolute refuge from fear, by revealing that all opposites and conflicting pairs are ultimately one. In this unified vision, there is nothing left to fear.

translit: cēkara māmpala citti nilaikkelām ākara māñcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the Sabai, which is the very source of all the many collected states of perfection.
commentary: All spiritual powers and perfections, the siddhis, have their source in this divine hall (Sabai). It is the fountainhead from which every perfected state arises.

translit: maṉātikaṭ kariya matātīta veḷiyām aṉāticiṟ capaiyi laruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the beginningless Hall of Consciousness, the transcendent expanse beyond all doctrines, incomprehensible to the mind and its faculties.
commentary: The ultimate reality of the Grace-Light cannot be understood by the rational mind or contained within any religion or philosophy. It is a timeless, infinite consciousness that must be experienced directly, as it exists far beyond the reach of our mental faculties.

translit: ōtiniṉ ṟuṇarntuṇarn tuṇartaṟ karitām āticiṟ capaiyi laruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the primordial Hall of Consciousness, which remains difficult to fully realize even after one studies, contemplates, and understands it again and again.
commentary: Spiritual realization is not a one-time achievement that can be mastered through study. Even with intense, repeated effort to understand the divine, its fullness remains just beyond our grasp, inviting us into a process of ever-deepening discovery.

translit: vāramu maḻiyā varamun taruntiru vāramu tāñcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the Hall that is sacred, abundant ambrosia, which bestows both love and an imperishable boon.
commentary: The experience of the divine consciousness is like a sacred ambrosia, a nourishing nectar for the soul. It bestows two essential gifts: profound love and a boon that is eternal and cannot be destroyed.

translit: iḻiyāp perunala mellā maḷittaruḷ aḻiyāc ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the imperishable Hall of Consciousness, which graciously grants all great and undiminishing good.
commentary: The divine consciousness itself is eternal and cannot be destroyed. It is the source from which all true and lasting goodness flows, a grace that is inexhaustible and never diminishes.

translit: kaṟpam palapala kaḻiyiṉu maḻivuṟā aṟputan taruñcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the Hall that bestows a wonder that does not perish, even as many, many eons pass.
commentary: The divine consciousness grants a state of being that is a true wonder because it stands outside of time. Even as entire cosmic cycles, or eons, pass away, the gift it bestows remains untouched and imperishable.

translit: eṉaittun tuṉpilā viyalaḷit teṇṇiya vaṉaittun taruñcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the Hall that grants a nature entirely free from suffering and gives everything that is thought of.
commentary: This inner Hall of Light has the power to transform your very nature, removing suffering at its root. It is also the source of all fulfillment, bringing to reality whatever the purified mind intends.

translit: pāṇip pilatāyp paraviṉōrk karuḷpuri āṇippo ṉampalat taruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the Hall of Pure Gold, who grants grace without delay to those who praise.
commentary: The divine response is not delayed; grace is given instantly to those who sincerely praise and seek it. The "Hall of Pure Gold" is a metaphor for the precious, incorruptible inner space where this connection happens.

translit: empala meṉattoḻu tēttiṉōrk karuḷpuri ampalat tāṭalcey yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which performs the dance in the Ambalam and grants grace to those who worship and praise it as "our strength."
commentary: The divine is not a static object but a dynamic, cosmic "dance" of energy and consciousness. When one recognizes this divine power as their only true strength, grace flows freely.

translit: tampara ñāṉa citampara meṉumōr amparat tōṅkiya aruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, risen high in the expanse called the Chidambaram of the Self's supreme wisdom.
commentary: The Grace-Light is found within you, in the "expanse of consciousness" known as Chidambaram. It shines most brightly in the state of supreme self-awareness, which is the ultimate wisdom.

translit: eccapai potuveṉa viyampiṉa raṟiñarkaḷ accapai yiṭaṅkoḷu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which takes as its place that very Hall which the wise have proclaimed to be the Common one.
commentary: This sacred Hall of Light is not a private or exclusive place. The truly wise of all traditions have recognized it as a "Common" space, accessible to every single being without distinction.

translit: vāṭuta ṉīkkiya maṇimaṉ ṟiṭaiyē āṭutal valla varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, skilled in dancing within the jeweled hall that banishes all withering.
commentary: God's grace is an active, joyful force that ends our suffering. Vallalar pictures this as a dance of the Divine Light within a "jeweled hall" in our consciousness, a dance whose very movement banishes all sorrow and withering.

translit: nāṭakat tirucceya ṉaviṟṟiṭu morupē rāṭakap potuvoḷi raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, shining in the one great golden common hall, enacting the sacred drama.
commentary: The entire universe is a sacred play enacted by God (Leela). This "great golden common hall" is the stage of creation itself, and everything that happens is part of a meaningful cosmic drama directed by the Divine Light.

translit: kaṟpaṉai muḻuvatum kaṭantoḷi tarumōr aṟputac ciṟcapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the wondrous Chit Sabhai, which transcends all imagination and bestows light.
commentary: The true nature of the Divine Light is found in the Chit Sabhai, the Hall of Consciousness within you, a reality that cannot be grasped by thought or imagination. To experience this wondrous light, you must go beyond the mind.

translit: īṉṟanaṟ ṟāyiṉu miṉiya peruntaya vāṉṟaciṟ capaiyi laruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi in the Chit Sabhai, filled with a great compassion sweeter even than that of the good mother who bore me.
commentary: The compassion of God is more intimate and sweet than even the love of the mother who gave birth to you. This immense tenderness is not distant but is the very nature of the Divine Light found within your own consciousness.

translit: iṉpuṟu nāṉuḷat teṇṇiyāṅ keṇṇiyāṅ kaṉpuṟat tarucapai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi of the hall, which lovingly grants things just as I, who am joyful, envision them in my heart.
commentary: When you are filled with joy and connected to the divine, your own pure intentions are lovingly brought to life. In this state of alignment, what you envision in your heart is granted, because your will has become one with the flow of grace.

translit: emmaiyu meṉṉaiviṭ ṭiṟaiyum piriyā tammaiyap paṉumā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is my Mother and Father, never parting from me for even an instant, in any birth.
commentary: The divine is not a distant ruler but an intimate, parental presence, embodying both motherly and fatherly qualities. This presence is constant and absolute, never absent for even a moment.

translit: pirivuṟ ṟaṟiyāp perumporu ḷāyeṉ ṉaṟivuk kaṟivā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the Great Reality that knows no separation, the intelligence within my own intelligence.
commentary: The nature of God is defined as the very intelligence that animates our own minds, the consciousness that allows us to be conscious. It is a reality so fundamental that separation from it is impossible.

translit: cātiyu matamuñ camayamuṅ kāṇā ātiya nātiyā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is the beginning and the beginningless, perceiving no caste, creed, or religion.
commentary: This is a core teaching: the ultimate reality, the Vast Grace-Light, is completely beyond the divisions of caste, religion, or any other social identity that humans create. It is a universal truth accessible to all, without prerequisite or label.

translit: tanukara ṇātika ṭāṅkaṭan taṟiyumōr anupava mākiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is the direct experience known by transcending the body, inner faculties, and all such things.
commentary: The path to knowing this Light is not through the intellect or the senses. It requires going beyond the limits of the physical body (tanu) and the mind's ordinary faculties (karanam) to attain a state of direct, unmediated experience (anubhavam).

translit: uṉumuṇar vuṇarvā yuṇarvelāṅ kaṭanta anupavā tīta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, the consciousness within the thinking consciousness, transcending all consciousness, a state beyond direct experience.
commentary: Here, Vallalar pushes into a profound paradox. The divine is the very consciousness that allows us to think, yet it also exists beyond all forms of consciousness we can know. After describing it as a direct experience, he now calls it anubhavātīta, a state that transcends even that experience, the ultimate source of all knowing.

translit: potuvuṇar vuṇarum pōtalāṟ pirittē atuveṉiṟ ṟōṉṟā varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is realized only through a universal consciousness and does not appear if singled out and pointed to as “that.”
commentary: The Grace-Light cannot be isolated or pointed to as a separate object. It is only realized through a unified, universal consciousness that sees the whole, not by trying to grasp a single part.

translit: uḷaviṉi laṟintā loḻiyamaṟ ṟaḷakkiṉ aḷaviṉi laḷavā varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which no measure can contain when one tries to measure it, and which is known only inwardly.
commentary: The mind cannot measure or contain the Grace-Light; it is infinite and beyond all concepts of quantity. It can only be known directly, as it is, not through our attempts to define or describe it.

translit: eṉṉaiyum paṇikoṇ ṭiṟavā varamaḷit taṉṉaiyi luvanta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which accepted even me into its service, granted the boon of immortality, and rejoiced more than a mother.
commentary: The Vast Grace-Light is an impersonal force and a loving presence that rejoices like a mother. Vallalar expresses his personal wonder that this ultimate reality accepted him, granting him the gift of immortality with a joy greater than any human affection.

translit: ōtiyō tāma luṟaveṉak kaḷitta ātiyī ṟillā varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, without beginning or end, which granted me a relationship with it without my having to study or recite.
commentary: A relationship with the eternal Grace-Light is a direct gift, not a reward for scriptural study or ritual recitation. Vallalar makes it clear that his own connection came freely, emphasizing that grace is accessible to anyone, regardless of their learning.

translit: paṭiyaṭi vāṉmuṭi paṟṟiṉun tōṟṟā aṭimuṭi yeṉumō raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, with a foot and a head that cannot be seen, even if one grasps the earth as its foot and the sky as its head.
commentary: The Grace-Light is so immense that even the entire cosmos cannot define its form. Trying to imagine the earth as its feet and the sky as its head still fails to capture its true, boundless nature, which is without beginning or end.

translit: pavaṉat tiṉaṇṭap parappiṉeṅ keṅkum avaṉuk kavaṉā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Everywhere in the expanse of the kinetic universe, Arutperunjothi is He for him.
commentary: For every being that conceives of the divine as masculine, the Grace-Light is the ultimate "He." It is the absolute reality that is the source and substance of every individual person or god perceived as male.

translit: tivaḷuṟ ṟavaṇṭat tiraḷiṉeṅ keṅkum avaḷuk kavaḷā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Everywhere in the cluster of radiant universes, Arutperunjothi is She for her.
commentary: Just as it is the ultimate "He," the Grace-Light is also the ultimate "She." It is the divine feminine principle, the source and reality for all who see God as a goddess or as feminine in nature.

translit: mataṉuṟṟa vaṇṭa varaippiṉeṅ keṅkum ataṉuk katuvā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Everywhere within the confines of the mighty universe, Arutperunjothi is It for it.
commentary: The Divine is not limited to masculine or feminine forms; it is also the ultimate "It." This completes the idea that the Grace-Light is the formless, genderless source of everything that exists, encompassing all beings and all ways of perceiving reality.

translit: eppālu māyveḷi yellāṅ kaṭantumēl appālu mākiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi is present in all realms, transcends all of space, and is what lies even beyond the beyond.
commentary: The Grace-Light is simultaneously everywhere within the universe and infinitely beyond it. It fills all known and unknown realms while also existing in a state that transcends space, time, and even the very concept of a "beyond."

translit: vallatā yellā mākiyel lāmum allatāy viḷaṅku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi shines, all-powerful, having become everything and yet being other than all things.
commentary: A core paradox: the all-powerful Divine Light becomes everything in the universe, yet it also remains completely distinct from its creation. It is the substance of all things, but it is not limited or defined by them.

translit: epporuḷ meypporu ḷeṉparmey kaṇṭōr apporu ḷākiya aruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi is the very substance that the truth-seers call the ultimate reality of all things.
commentary: Those who have seen the deepest truth, the great sages and seers, all point to the same reality. The ultimate substance behind all things, the "true thing" (meypporuḷ), is this Vast Grace-Light.

translit: tāṅkaki lāṇṭa carācara nilainiṉ ṟāṅkuṟa viḷaṅku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi abides, supporting all universes with their moving and unmoving beings, shining forth perfectly.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the foundation that supports all of creation. It sustains every universe, along with every moving creature and every unmoving thing like plants and mountains, allowing them to exist.

translit: cattarka ḷellān taḻaittiṭa vakampuṟat tatticai viḷaṅku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi shines within, without, and in every direction, making all the Saktars flourish.
commentary: The Grace-Light is what empowers the Saktars, who are masters of divine power and spiritual attainment. It nourishes them from within and without, causing their spiritual strength to thrive in all directions.

translit: cattika ḷellān taḻaikkaveṅ keṅkum attakai viḷaṅku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi shines everywhere in such a way that all the Saktis flourish.
commentary: Just as it empowers enlightened beings, the Grace-Light is also the source from which all divine energies, or Saktis, draw their vitality. It is the universal force that makes all other cosmic forces flourish.

translit: muntuṟu maintoḻiṉ mūrttikaḷ palarkkum aintoḻi laḷikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi grants the five functions to the many deities who perform those primary five functions.
commentary: Even the great deities who are traditionally said to perform the five cosmic functions (creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and grace) are not the ultimate source of that power. The Grace-Light is the true origin, granting them the ability to perform these roles.

translit: peritiṉum peritāyc ciṟitiṉuñ ciṟitāy aritiṉu maritā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Greater than the greatest, smaller than the smallest, rarer than the rarest, is the Vast Grace-Light.
commentary: The Divine is both bigger than the biggest thing imaginable and smaller than the smallest particle, existing beyond all categories of human thought. This paradox describes a reality that is simultaneously everywhere and nowhere, a presence that fills the entire cosmos yet can be found within the tiniest atom.

translit: kāṭciyuṅ kāṇāk kāṭciyu matutarum āṭciyu mākiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: The seen vision, the unseen vision, and the mastery they bestow, is the Vast Grace-Light.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the thing you see in a spiritual vision and the very capacity to see it. It is both the external experience of the divine and the internal, formless knowing. Finally, it is the spiritual authority and power that comes from this dual perception.

translit: iṉpuṟu cittika ḷellām purikaveṉ ṟaṉpuṭa ṉeṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which with love graciously commanded me: "Perform all blissful siddhis."
commentary: The Grace-Light itself commanded Vallalar to exercise siddhis, which are supernatural abilities like healing or transforming matter. Crucially, this command is given with love, and the powers are described as blissful, suggesting their purpose is not for personal gain but for demonstrating the power of grace.

translit: iṟavā varamaḷit teṉṉaimē lēṟṟiya aṟavāḻi yāntaṉi yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: The singular Vast Grace-Light, an ocean of virtue, which granted me the boon of immortality and elevated me.
commentary: Here, Vallalar makes a central claim of his teaching: the Grace-Light has given him the gift of immortality. This is a spiritual afterlife and a transformation of the physical body into a deathless state, an ultimate elevation of human potential made possible by divine grace.

translit: nāṉanta millā nalampeṟa veṉakkē āṉanta nalkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestowed bliss upon me so I may attain endless good.
commentary: The experience of divine bliss is not an end in itself. Vallalar states that the Jothi granted him bliss for a specific reason: to empower him to achieve and share "endless good," linking personal spiritual attainment directly to a mission of universal welfare.

translit: eṇṇiya veṇṇiyāṅ kiyaṟṟuka veṉṟeṉai yaṇṇiyuḷ ḷōṅku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you drew near, rose within me, and told me, “Whatever you have thought, carry it out.”
commentary: The divine light does not command, but empowers. By affirming Vallalar's own thoughts and giving him the authority to act on them, grace validates his inner compass and trusts him to carry out his mission.

translit: mēyiṉai meypporuḷ viḷaṅkiṉai nīyatu vāyiṉai yeṉṟaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graced me, saying, “You have reached the True Substance, you have understood it, you have become That itself.”
commentary: Grace reveals the final truth of spiritual union: the self is no longer separate from God, but has become God. This is the moment where all distinction dissolves, and the individual realizes their own nature is the same as the ultimate reality, the "True Substance."

translit: eṇṇiṟ ceḻuntē ṉiṉiyateḷ ḷamuteṉa aṇṇit tiṉikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, when thought of, draws near and is sweet as rich honey and sweet, clear nectar.
commentary: The divine presence is not an abstract idea but a tangible, sensory experience. Grace is a sweetness that fills the mind, as real and delightful as rich honey or the clarifying nectar of ambrosia.

translit: cintaiyiṟ ṟuṉpoḻi civampeṟu keṉattoḻi laintaiyu meṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you graced me with the five cosmic functions, saying, “Rid your mind of suffering and attain Sivam.”
commentary: To achieve Sivam (the ultimate state of auspiciousness), the mind must be free from suffering. Here, the Grace-Light bestows the five cosmic functions traditionally seen as God's own: creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and grace. This is a profound transfer of divine power, equipping the soul to act as a direct agent of grace in the world.

translit: eṅkeṅ kiruntuyi rētetu vēṇṭiṉum aṅkaṅ kiruntaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Wherever a soul may be and whatever it may desire, you are present there, bestowing grace, Arutperunjothi.
commentary: The Grace-Light is not a remote deity, but a presence that is everywhere at once. It meets every soul exactly where it is, responding to its specific needs and desires with immediate, personal grace.

translit: cakamutaṟ puṟappuṟan taṅkiya vakappuṟam akampuṟa muṟṟumā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which abides in the outermost world, the first to arise, and has become the entire inner-exterior and the complete interior-and-exterior.
commentary: The Grace-Light permeates every possible level of existence. It is present in the outermost physical world, in the intermediate realms that are both inner and outer, and in the purely internal world of consciousness itself. There is no place or dimension, from the most physical to the most subtle, where the Light is not.

translit: cikaramum vakaramuñ cērtaṉi yukaramum akaramu mākiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is the letter 'si', the letter 'va', the solitary joining letter 'u', and the letter 'a'.
commentary: The Grace-Light is identified with the fundamental sounds that form sacred names. It is the letters 'si' and 'va' which form the name Siva, and also the primordial sounds 'a' and 'u' which are core components of the universal sound 'Om'. The Light is more than described by these sounds; it is them.

translit: uparaca vētiyi ṉupayamum paramum aparamu mākiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, in the alchemy of secondary substances, is the pair, the supreme, and the non-supreme.
commentary: In the world of Siddha alchemy, which seeks to transmute base substances into perfected ones, the Grace-Light is the hidden principle that makes transformation possible. It is the opposing elements (ubayam, the pair), the refined final product (param, the supreme), and the raw starting material (aparam, the non-supreme). The Light encompasses every stage of the process, from lowest to highest.

translit: mantaṇa mituveṉa maṟuvilā matiyāl antaṇar vaḻuttu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which the virtuous ones (antaṇar: traditionally brahmins, here meaning the truly virtuous) praise with flawless wisdom, declaring, 'This is the secret'.
commentary: The true sages, those with pure hearts and clear minds, recognize the Grace-Light as the ultimate secret of existence. Here, the term antaṇar is redefined from its traditional meaning of a brahmin by birth to mean anyone who is genuinely virtuous and compassionate. It is these people, regardless of background, who possess the wisdom to see the Light and praise it as the final truth.

translit: empuyak kaṉiyeṉa veṇṇuvā ritaya vampuyat tamarnta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, resting in the heart-lotus of those who regard it as the precious fruit borne upon their shoulders.
commentary: The Grace-Light dwells within the hearts of those who treasure it intimately. The image of a "fruit borne upon our shoulders" suggests something precious, personal, and carried with constant awareness and affection. For those who hold the Light in such high esteem, it is not a distant concept but a living presence in their heart-lotus (itaya vampuyam).

translit: ceṭiyaṟut tētiṭa tēkamum pōkamum aṭiyaruk kētaru maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi severs all impurities and grants a perfected body and its enjoyment exclusively to devotees.
commentary: The Grace-Light (Arutperunjothi) cleanses a person of all that is impure. This purification extends to the physical body (dēham), transforming it into a perfected form capable of experiencing a divine kind of enjoyment (bhōgam). For Vallalar, the body is not an obstacle to be escaped, but a vessel to be divinized.

translit: tuṉpaṟut toruciva turiya cukantaṉai aṉparuk kētaru maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi severs all suffering and grants the bliss of the singular Siva-Turiya exclusively to those who love it.
commentary: By connecting with the Grace-Light, all suffering is cut away. In its place, one is given the bliss of Siva-Turiya, a state of pure consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, where the soul experiences its unity with the divine. The only requirement for this supreme state is love.

translit: potuvatu ciṟappatu putiyatu paḻayateṉ ṟatuvatu vāyttika ḻaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi shines, itself being that which is general and that which is special, that which is new and that which is old.
commentary: The Grace-Light resolves all apparent opposites. It is simultaneously the universal principle common to all and the particular, unique experience. It is the most ancient, timeless reality and is also perpetually fresh and new in its revelation.

translit: cētaṉap perunilai tikaḻtaru moruparai yātaṉat tōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi is exalted upon the throne of the one Parai, who manifests the great state of consciousness.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the ultimate reality, resting upon the power of Parai, the supreme divine feminine energy. She is the one who brings forth all states of consciousness, and her power serves as the very foundation or "throne" for the expression of the formless Light.

translit: ōmayat tiruvuru vuvappuṭa ṉaḷitteṉak kāmayat taṭaitavi raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi joyfully grants me the sacred form that is the essence of Om, and removes the obstacle of my disease.
commentary: Here, the teaching becomes intensely personal. The Grace-Light cures the soul and the body, removing Vallalar's physical illness. It can replace the mortal form with a "sacred form" whose very substance is Om, the primordial vibration of existence.

translit: eppaṭi yeṇṇiya teṉkarut tiṅkeṉak kappaṭi yaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which granted to me here exactly what my mind conceived.
commentary: The divine grace has fulfilled every specific thought Vallalar has ever held. His inner world of intention is perfectly mirrored by the outer reality created by grace.

translit: ettakai viḻaintaṉa veṉmaṉa miṅkeṉak kattakai yaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which granted to me here whatever my mind desired.
commentary: Expanding on the previous line, Vallalar says that grace grants his specific thoughts and his deepest desires. There is a complete alignment between his personal will and the will of the divine.

translit: iṅkuṟat tirintuḷa miḷaiyā vakaiyeṉak kaṅkaiyiṟ kaṉiyā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which became a ripe fruit in my palm so my heart would not grow weary from wandering here.
commentary: After a long search that wearied his heart, the grace he sought became something concrete and immediate. It is like a ripe fruit placed directly in his hand, a tangible gift, not a distant concept.

translit: pāruyap purikeṉap paṇitteṉak karuḷiyeṉ āruyirk kuḷḷoḷi raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which commanded me, "Act to uplift the world," and, granting grace, shines within my own precious life.
commentary: Receiving grace is not the end of the journey; it is the beginning of a mission. The divine light shines within him with a clear command: now, work to uplift the entire world.

translit: tēviyuṟ ṟoḷirtaru tiruvuru vuṭaṉeṉa tāviyiṟ kalantoḷi raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, with a sacred form radiant with the Goddess, has mingled into my soul and shines.
commentary: The divine Grace-Light is more than an abstract concept; it can manifest with a form, radiant with the presence of the Goddess (the divine feminine). This divine reality, uniting masculine and feminine principles, has intimately merged with Vallalar's own being.

translit: evvaḻi meyvaḻi yeṉpavē tākamam avvaḻi yeṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graced me with the very path that the Vedas and Agamas declare to be the true path.
commentary: The Grace-Light has revealed the true path directly to him, confirming the highest truth found in the ancient scriptures known as the Vedas and Agamas. His path is therefore not a new invention but the very essence of timeless wisdom, now made accessible through direct experience.

translit: vaiyamum vāṉamum vāḻttiṭa veṉakkaruḷ aiyaṟi vaḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestowed upon me the five forms of knowledge, for the world and the heavens to praise.
commentary: The Grace-Light has granted a complete, divine understanding that transcends ordinary human knowledge. This gift, which he calls the "five forms of knowledge" (aiyaṟivu), elevates his consciousness to a level that beings on both earth and in heavenly realms can recognize and praise.

translit: cāmā ṟaṉaittun tavirttiṅ keṉakkē āmā ṟaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, removing for me every way of dying, has graced me here with the way to thrive.
commentary: Here is the promise of physical immortality. The Grace-Light has removed all causes of death and decay, replacing them with a state of perpetual existence and flourishing. It is a complete victory over mortality, a core goal of Vallalar's path.

translit: cattiya māñciva cattiyai yīnteṉak kattiṟal vaḷarkku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which gave me the true Siva-Sakti and develops that strength within me.
commentary: The Grace-Light has infused him with true Siva-Sakti, the dynamic and creative power of the divine. This is not a static gift; the Light continuously nurtures and strengthens this divine power within him, transforming him into a vessel of God's own creative force.

translit: cāvā nilaiyitu tantaṉa muṉakkē āvā veṉavaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestows grace with an exclamation of "Ah!" and says, "This deathless state I have given to you alone."
commentary: God's grace is portrayed here as a deeply personal and joyful act. The exclamation "Ah!" suggests a spontaneous, loving wonder, while the declaration "I have given to you alone" highlights the intimate, one-to-one relationship between the soul and the Divine.

translit: cātiyu matamuñ camayamum poyyeṉa ātiyi luṇarttiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which taught from the very beginning that caste, religion, and denomination are false.
commentary: This is one of Vallalar's most direct teachings: all social and religious divisions are human inventions that are ultimately false. From the very beginning, the divine light reveals a truth that transcends caste, religion, and denomination.

translit: mayarntiṭēl ciṟitu maṉantaḷarn tañcēl ayarntiṭē leṉṟaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestows grace, saying: "Do not be bewildered, not even a little. Do not let your mind falter and fear. Do not grow weary."
commentary: The divine is not a silent, distant presence but a source of constant, gentle encouragement. This verse captures the voice of grace speaking directly to the devotee's deepest anxieties, offering personal reassurance not to fear or falter.

translit: tēcuṟat tikaḻtaru tiruneṟip poruḷiyal ācaṟat teritta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which flawlessly revealed the true nature of the substance of the Sacred Path, which shines with splendor.
commentary: The spiritual path is a set of rules or ideas and a glorious reality with its own luminous essence. The Vast Grace-Light (Arutperunjothi) makes the true nature of this path perfectly clear, removing all doubts and misconceptions.

translit: kāṭṭiya vulakelāṅ karuṇaiyāṟ cittiyiṉ āṭṭiyal puriyu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, out of compassion, performs the dance of siddhi in all the manifested worlds.
commentary: The workings of the universe are a divine dance. This cosmic activity, which manifests as siddhi (spiritual perfections and powers), is not random but is a continuous performance driven by compassion for all beings.

translit: eṅkula memmiṉa meṉpatoṇ ṇūṟṟā ṟaṅkula meṉṟaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously declared that our lineage and our race are the ninety-six angulams (the traditional measure of the human body).
commentary: Vallalar offers a new definition of human identity that erases all social divisions. Our true lineage and race, he says, have nothing to do with family, caste, or nation; they are simply the physical reality of our human body, represented by its traditional measure of ninety-six angulams. Our shared humanity is the only tribe that matters.

translit: emmata memmiṟai yeṉpa vuyirttiraḷ ammata meṉṟaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, when asked "What is our religion? Who is our God?", graciously replied that the collective of all beings is itself the religion.
commentary: Here, Vallalar redefines religion itself. When asked what our path or god should be, the answer is not a doctrine or a deity, but the community of all living beings. The focus of spiritual life is shifted from abstract belief to our relationship with the collective whole of life.

translit: kūṟiya karunilai kulaviya kīḻmēl āṟiya leṉavurai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which proclaimed that the primordial source-state, which manifests both low and high, is the very nature of the six religious systems.
commentary: All the world's diverse religions, whether they seem "high" or "low," spring from a single, primordial source. Vallalar points to a unity underlying all spiritual paths, suggesting that each is simply a different expression of the same ultimate reality.

translit: eṇṭara muṭiyā tilaṅkiya paṟpala aṇṭamu niṟaintoḷi raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which fills and illuminates the innumerable, resplendent, and varied universes.
commentary: The divine light is not limited to this world; it is a cosmic reality. It fills and illuminates countless universes, each one unique and brilliant, establishing its presence as a universal, all-pervading consciousness.

translit: cāruyirk kellān tāraka māmparai yāruyirk kuyirā maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is Parai, the substratum for all embodied lives, and the very Life within each precious life.
commentary: The divine is both the foundation of our existence and the very essence of our life. It is Parai (the Supreme Power), the ultimate support for all beings, and at the same time, it is the intimate spark of life within each individual soul.

translit: vāḻinī ṭūḻi vāḻiyeṉ ṟōṅkupē rāḻiyai yaḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestowed the great decree, "Live long! Live for eons! Live!"
commentary: The ultimate command from God is a blessing for long life and endurance. This as a source of benevolent power that wants all beings to thrive.

translit: māyntavar mīṭṭum varuneṟi tantitai yāyntiṭeṉ ṟuraitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which provided the way for the dead to return and instructed, "Examine this."
commentary: This is one of Vallalar's revolutionary teachings: that death is not final and the divine has revealed a way to reverse it. The instruction to "Examine this" suggests this is not a matter of blind faith, but something that can be investigated and understood.

translit: eccani ṉakkilai yellām perukaveṉṟu accan tavirttaveṉ ṉaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: My Arutperunjothi, which removed my fear, saying, "You have no lack; may everything increase."
commentary: Fear often comes from a sense of lack or scarcity. Here, the divine voice removes fear by declaring the opposite: you lack nothing, and everything good in you will only grow. It's a fundamental shift from a mindset of deficit to one of abundance.

translit: nīṭuka nīyē nīḷula kaṉaittumniṉ ṟāṭuka veṉṟaveṉ ṉaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: My Arutperunjothi, which said, "Endure forever! Stand and dance throughout all the vast worlds."
commentary: Immortality here is not a passive, static state. It is an invitation to participate actively and joyfully in the cosmic dance, moving freely through all worlds with enduring energy.

translit: muttiṟal vaṭivamu muṉṉiyāṅ keytuṟu mattiṟa leṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestowed on me the power to attain the three potent forms just by intending it.
commentary: This refers to the power to transform one's own physical and subtle nature. Through grace, the practitioner gains the ability to manifest different bodies or states of being simply by the power of their intention, a sign of complete spiritual mastery.

translit: mūvakaic cittiyiṉ muṭipukaḷ muḻuvatum āvakai yeṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously made it possible for me to realize all the final results of the three types of siddhi.
commentary: Grace bestows spiritual insight and the full range of supernatural abilities, known as siddhi. These powers are not seen as obstacles but as natural results of divine realization.

translit: karumacit tikaḷiṉ kalaipala kōṭiyum aracuṟa veṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously gave me dominion over the countless arts of Karma Siddhi.
commentary: The first category of these powers is Karma Siddhi, or attainments achieved through action and ritual. Vallalar states that grace has given him complete mastery over the countless powers related to manipulating cause and effect in the world.

translit: yōkacit tikaḷvakai yuṟupala kōṭiyum ākaveṉ ṟeṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which granted me the countless varieties of Yoga Siddhi, saying, 'Let them be so.'
commentary: The second category is Yoga Siddhi, or powers gained through the discipline of mind and body. Grace has bestowed these abilities directly and effortlessly, granting the fruits of intense practice without the need for the long effort usually required.

translit: ñāṉacit tiyiṉvakai nalviri vaṉaittum āṉiyiṉ ṟeṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which flawlessly granted me all the fine, expansive varieties of Jnana Siddhi.
commentary: The third and highest category is Jnana Siddhi, or powers that arise directly from wisdom (jnana). These are the abilities that flow from a perfect, unmediated understanding of reality, granted flawlessly by grace.

translit: puṭaiyuṟu cittiyiṉ poruṭṭē muttiyai aṭaivateṉ ṟaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously declared that one attains mukti precisely for the sake of the siddhi that accompanies it.
commentary: Many traditions teach that liberation, or mukti, is the final goal, and supernatural powers (siddhi) are distractions on the way. Vallalar states the opposite: liberation is the means, and the powers are the purpose. One becomes free in order to be able to act in the world with divine power, serving and transforming life.

translit: muttiyeṉ patunilai muṉṉuṟu cātaṉam attaka veṉṟaveṉ ṉaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: My Arutperunjothi, which declared that mutti is the means that comes before the state.
commentary: Liberation (mutti) is not the end. Vallalar says it is the means (sādhanam) that comes before the true state, siddhi: the perfection of a deathless life in grace.

translit: cittiyeṉ patunilai cērnta vanupavam attiṟa leṉṟaveṉ ṉaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: My Arutperunjothi, which declared that siddhi is the experience of having reached that state, and its power.
commentary: Divine perfection (siddhi) is the lived experience (anubhavam) of the state itself, together with the power that comes with it. It is not an abstract achievement.

translit: ēkaciṟ cittiyē yiyaluṟa vaṉēkam ākiya teṉṟaveṉ ṉaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: My Arutperunjothi, which declared that the one perfection of consciousness (cit-siddhi) itself naturally became many.
commentary: The source of all divine powers is a single, unified state: the perfection of consciousness itself (cit-siddhi). From this one fundamental perfection, all the many different kinds of spiritual abilities naturally unfold.

translit: iṉpacit tiyiṉiya lēka maṉēkam aṉparuk keṉṟaveṉ ṉaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: My Arutperunjothi, which declared that for devotees, the nature of the perfection of bliss (inba-siddhi) is both one and many.
commentary: For true devotees (anbar), the perfection of bliss (inba-siddhi) is experienced in a special way. It is a single, ultimate joy, yet it manifests as countless different blissful experiences, each unique to the individual's relationship with the divine.

translit: eṭṭiraṇ ṭeṉpaṉa viyalumuṟ paṭiyeṉa aṭṭaniṉ ṟaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, standing firm, graciously ordained that the 'eight and two' are the natural steps.
commentary: The phrase 'eight and two' is a mystical code common in Tamil spiritual traditions. It refers to the sacred syllable AUM, because the Tamil characters for 'a' (அ) and 'u' (உ) resemble the shapes of the numbers eight (எ) and two (உ). The verse states that this primordial sound represents the foundational steps on the spiritual path.

translit: ippaṭi kaṇṭaṉai yiṉiyuṟu paṭiyelām appaṭi yēyeṉu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which affirmed, "You have seen it thus; all the steps to be experienced hereafter are exactly so."
commentary: This is a moment of divine confirmation for Vallalar's journey. The Grace-Light (Arutperunjothi) affirms that the ecstatic states and visions he has experienced are not delusions but are authentic and true.

translit: paṭimuṭi kaṭantaṉai pāritu pāreṉa aṭimuṭi kāṭṭiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which showed me its foot and its crown, saying, "You have transcended the world's limits; look at this, look!"
commentary: Showing the 'foot and the crown' is a classic way of revealing the entirety of God's being, from the lowest point to the highest. By granting this complete vision, the Divine acknowledges that Vallalar has transcended worldly consciousness and is ready to perceive the whole of reality.

translit: jōtiyuṭ jōtiyiṉ corupamē yanta mātiyeṉ ṟaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously declared that the very nature of the Light within the Light is the end and the beginning.
commentary: There is a deeper reality within the Divine Light itself. The verse describes this as a "Light within the Light," whose essential nature (sorupam) is the very source from which all creation emerges and the ultimate destination to which it returns.

translit: intaciṟ jōtiyi ṉiyaluru vāti yantameṉ ṟaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously declared that the inherent form of this Light of Consciousness is the beginning and the end.
commentary: The ultimate reality is not an abstract void but a "Light of Consciousness" (cit-jothi) with a true form. This conscious, luminous form is itself the beginning and the end of all existence.

translit: ātiyu mantamu maṟintaṉai nīyē ātiyeṉ ṟaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously declared, "You yourself have perceived the beginning and the end; you are the beginning."
commentary: This is a powerful statement of union between the devotee and the divine. Because Vallalar has truly perceived God as the beginning and end, God declares that he has become one with that source. The journey to see the divine culminates in the realization that the divine nature is one's own.

translit: nallamu teṉṉoru nāvuḷaṅ kāṭṭiyeṉ allalai nīkkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which revealed fine nectar to my tongue and heart, removing my suffering.
commentary: Divine grace is experienced as a tangible sweetness, a nectar (amuthu) that brings bliss and ends suffering. This gift is total, satisfying both the physical body and the inner mind.

translit: kaṟpaka meṉṉuḷaṅ kaitaṉiṟ koṭuttē aṟputa miyaṟṟeṉu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which placed the Karpagam in the palm of my hand and commanded, "Perform miracles."
commentary: The Karpagam, a mythical tree from celestial realms that grants any wish, symbolizes the infinite potential bestowed by grace. The Light does more than give this power; it commands Vallalar to use it to perform miracles, turning personal transformation into a mission of public good.

translit: katirnala meṉṉiru kaṇkaḷiṟ koṭuttē aticaya miyaṟṟeṉu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which placed radiant virtue in my two eyes and commanded, "Perform wonders."
commentary: Grace transforms one's very perception, making the eyes instruments of divine power. Vallalar's sight becomes a source of benevolent energy, capable of creating wonders in the world. Again, this gift comes with a command to act.

translit: aruḷoḷi yeṉṟaṉi yaṟiviṉil virittē aruṇeṟi viḷakkeṉu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which spread the light of Grace in my unique intellect and commanded, "Illuminate the path of Grace."
commentary: The Divine Light fills Vallalar's mind with its own clarity. He is then instructed to become a beacon for others, using his enlightened intellect to illuminate the path of grace for all of humanity.

translit: paraiyoḷi yeṉmaṉap patiyiṉil virittē aracatu viyaṟṟeṉu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which spread the light of Parai in the seat of my mind and commanded, "Exercise your sovereignty."
commentary: The light of Parai, the supreme creative power of the cosmos, is established within Vallalar's mind. The command to "exercise sovereignty" signifies the attainment of complete spiritual authority and self-mastery, entrusting him with the full power of grace.

translit: vallapa cattikaḷ vakaiyelā maḷitteṉa tallalai nīkkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which granted every kind of masterful power and dispelled my distress.
commentary: Gaining divine power is what finally ends all suffering. The Grace-Light grants every kind of vallabha shakti (masterful power), and through this empowerment, it completely removes the distress that once defined his life.

translit: āriya lakampuṟa makappuṟam puṟappuṟam āramu teṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously gave me the supreme ambrosia of the inner, outer, inner-outer, and outer-outer realms.
commentary: The experience of divine bliss is total, filling every layer of existence. Grace gives him the supreme ambrosia inwardly (aham) and in the outer world (puṟam) and in the realms that connect them, integrating his entire reality in sweetness.

translit: cūriya cantira jōtiyuṭ jōtiyeṉ ṟāriyar pukaḻtaru maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which the wise praise as the Light within the light of the sun and moon.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the source of all other lights, both physical and subtle. The wise (āriyar) recognize that even the powerful light of the sun and moon is just a reflection of this ultimate inner radiance.

translit: piṟivē tiṉiyuṉaip piṭittaṉa muṉakkunam maṟivē vaṭiveṉu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which declared, “What separation is there now? We have taken hold of you; for you, our consciousness is your form.”
commentary: The ultimate union with God is a total transformation of one's own being. Once separation is overcome, the divine itself declares that its own consciousness (aṟivu) has now become Vallalar's very form.

translit: eñcē lulakiṉil yātoṉṟu paṟṟiyum añcē leṉṟaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously commands, "Do not falter in the world over anything at all, and do not fear."
commentary: The final fruit of spiritual realization is absolute fearlessness. The Grace-Light gives a direct, simple command: live in the world without faltering or being afraid of anything.

translit: māṇṭuḻa lāvakai vantiḷaṅ kālaiyē āṇṭukoṇ ṭaruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which came in my youth and graciously made me its own, so that I would not perish and wander.
commentary: Grace came to him when he was young, setting him on a spiritual path and saving him from the ordinary fate of wandering through life only to perish. This early intervention is seen as a profound act of compassion, preventing a life wasted in confusion.

translit: paṟṟuka ḷaṉaittaiyum paṟṟaṟat tavirtteṉa taṟṟamu nīkkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which completely severed all my attachments and removed my deficiencies.
commentary: The path to spiritual freedom requires letting go of all attachments, and the Grace-Light itself performs this act of liberation. It removes our external dependencies and our inner imperfections, purifying us completely.

translit: camayaṅ kulamutaṟ cārpelām viṭutta amayan tōṉṟiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which appeared at the opportune moment, once I had abandoned all affiliations starting with religion and caste.
commentary: This is a core teaching for Vallalar. The Grace-Light only revealed itself to him after he had moved beyond all limiting identities like organized religion, family lineage, and social caste. True spiritual experience happens in a space free from these human-made divisions.

translit: vāytaṟ kuritteṉu maṟaiyā kamaṅkaḷāl āytaṟ kariya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which is impossible to investigate by means of the Vedas and Agamas, which are held to be the authoritative means.
commentary: The experience of the Grace-Light is beyond intellectual understanding or scriptural debate. Even the most revered holy texts, the Vedas (hymns and philosophical treatises) and Agamas (manuals for ritual and worship), cannot truly describe or analyze it. It must be experienced directly.

translit: ellām vallacit teṉakkaḷit teṉakkuṉai yallā tilaiyeṉu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which granted me the siddhi that can do all things and declared, “For Me, there is none other than you.”
commentary: The Grace-Light gives the siddhi that can do all things, and with it a declaration of intimacy: God claims the soul so wholly that God says, “For Me, there is none other than you.”

translit: navaiyilā vuḷatti ṉāṭiya nāṭiya vavaiyelā maḷikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which grants everything sought within a flawless heart.
commentary: The key to receiving what you truly need from God is not elaborate prayer, but a pure and faultless heart. When your intention is clear and selfless, grace fulfills that need.

translit: kūṟṟutait teṉpāṟ kuṟṟamuṅ kuṇaṅkoṇ ṭāṟṟaṉmik kaḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which kicked away Death, took even my faults as virtues, and granted me abundant power.
commentary: God's grace is so powerful it can conquer death itself. In a remarkable expression of love, it does forgive his flaws and accepts them as if they were virtues, transforming them into a source of strength.

translit: naṉṟaṟi vaṟiyā nāyiṉēṉ ṟaṉaiyum aṉṟuvan tāṇṭa varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which came that day and graciously took in even me, a dog who does not know what is good.
commentary: In a state of deep humility, Vallalar sees himself as a mere dog, ignorant of what is truly good. Yet even in that state, God's grace came to him and claimed him as its own.

translit: nāyiṉuṅ kaṭaiyē ṉīyiṉu miḻintēṉ āyiṉu maruḷiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which showed me grace even though I am lower than a dog and more wretched than a fly.
commentary: The feeling of humility deepens even further. Vallalar feels lower than a dog, more insignificant than a fly, yet grace still reached him. The point is that divine compassion is not earned through merit; it is given freely, even to those who feel most worthless.

translit: tōttiram pukalēṉ pāttira mallēṉ āttira maḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which gave me intense longing, though I do not recite hymns of praise and am not a worthy vessel.
commentary: One does not need to be a perfect devotee to receive grace. Vallalar admits he fails at the basics, feeling unworthy and unable to even offer proper praise. Yet God gave him the most important gift: an intense, burning desire for the divine.

translit: eccō taṉaikaḷu miyaṟṟā teṉakkē accō veṉṟaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which spares me from all trials, saying "Oh, alas!" and granting me grace.
commentary: The phrase "Oh, alas!" reveals a tender, almost parental quality in the divine. It suggests that the Arutperunjothi (Vast Grace-Light) is not a distant, unfeeling force. Instead, it feels the soul's potential suffering so deeply that it intervenes to prevent it, acting out of pure empathy.

translit: ēṟā nilainaṭu vēṟṟiyeṉ ṟaṉaiyīṇ ṭāṟāṟu kaṭattiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which elevated me to the center of the state that is impossible to ascend, and made me transcend the thirty-six tattvas here.
commentary: The "thirty-six tattvas" are the fundamental principles making up the universe and our body, from physical elements to the subtle levels of mind. To transcend them is to go beyond all created reality. Vallalar states this is "impossible to ascend" by one's own power; it can only be reached when grace itself, the Arutperunjothi, lifts you there.

translit: tāpat tuyaran tavirttula kuṟumelā āpattum nīkkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which ended the misery of afflictions and removed all the worldly calamities.
commentary: Divine grace operates on two levels at once. It heals internal suffering like mental anguish and spiritual doubt, while also protecting from external dangers and disasters. For Vallalar, spiritual freedom means a complete end to all forms of suffering, both inner and outer.

translit: maruṭpakai tavirtteṉai vāḻvit teṉakkē yaruṭkuru vākiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which dispelled the enemy of delusion, made me thrive, and became the Guru of Grace for me.
commentary: The greatest obstacle to spiritual life is maruḷ (delusion), the fundamental ignorance that binds us. Here, the divine light, Arutperunjothi, acts directly as the Arut-Guru (the Teacher of Grace), dispelling this darkness without the need for an external human teacher. Once confusion is gone, the soul naturally begins to thrive.

translit: uruvamu maruvamu mupayamu mākiya aruṇilai teritta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which revealed the state of grace that is form, formlessness, and both combined.
commentary: People often debate whether God has a form or is formless. Vallalar says the ultimate state of grace transcends this argument. It can be experienced with form (uruvam), without form (aruvam), and in a way that is both at once. The divine is not confined by human concepts.

translit: iruḷaṟut teṉṉuḷat teṇṇiyāṅ karuḷi aruḷamu taḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which cut away the darkness, graciously acted according to my heart's conception, and bestowed the nectar of grace.
commentary: The divine Grace-Light does more than impose its will; it meets us where we are and manifests according to our own deepest, purest conception of it. This personal relationship then bestows the "nectar of grace," a taste of immortal sweetness

translit: teruṇilai yituveṉat teruṭṭiyeṉ ṉuḷattiruntuḷa aruṇilai kāṭṭiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which clarified for me, "This is the state of clarity," and, residing in my heart, revealed the state of grace within.
commentary: Spiritual clarity is not an intellectual conclusion but a direct revelation from the grace residing within us. The Grace-Light itself points out the true state of being, removing all doubt from within the heart.

translit: poruṭpata mellām purintumē lōṅkiya aruṭpata maḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestowed the state of grace, which is exalted above all comprehended states of being.
commentary: The state of grace is the ultimate reality, surpassing every other level of existence or spiritual attainment that the mind can grasp. It is the final destination, higher than any heaven or realm one could imagine.

translit: uruḷcaka ṭākiya vuḷañcali yāvakai aruḷvaḻi niṟuttiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which steadied my mind, which was like a rolling wheel, upon the path of grace so it would not be shaken.
