translation: Arutperunjothi, which densely established the summit within the summit and the summit of the very summit.
commentary: Just as it is the ultimate foundation, the Grace-Light is also the absolute summit. It is the highest point of attainment, the peak that lies beyond all other peaks.

translit: akappū vakavuṟup pākka vataṟkavai akattē vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which created the parts of the inner world, fashioning them within.
commentary: The "inner world" refers to the subtle, internal aspects of our being: our mind, consciousness, and all our faculties of experience. The Grace-Light is the creative force that forms this entire inner landscape from within.

translit: puṟappū puṟattiṟ puṉaiyuru vākkiṭa aṟattuṭaṉ vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, with righteousness, fashioned the adorned forms of the outer world.
commentary: The "outer world" is the physical realm we perceive with our senses. The Grace-Light fashions all these external forms, and it does so according to aṟam (righteousness or cosmic order), implying that the physical universe is imbued with a fundamental moral and structural integrity.

translit: akappuṟap pūvakap puṟavuṟup piyaṟṟiṭa akattiṭai vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which created the parts of the inner-outer world, fashioning them within.
commentary: The "inner-outer world" refers to the faculties that connect our inner experience to the outer world, such as our sense organs and motor functions. The Grace-Light creates these instruments that allow us to perceive and interact with physical reality.

translit: puṟappuṟap pūvatiṟ puṟappuṟa vuṟuppuṟa aṟattiṭai vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which righteously established the outermost parts within the outermost world.
commentary: The Grace-Light's creative power reaches the outermost, most tangible realm (puṟappuṟam). Here pū means the world, not a flower: even the outermost parts of the physical world are set in a righteous order.

translit: pāriṭai vērvaiyiṟ paiyiṭai muṭṭaiyil āruyi ramaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which fashions precious life from the earth, from sweat, from the womb, and from the egg.
commentary: All life, regardless of how it begins, originates from the Grace-Light. The verse lists the four traditional categories of birth: from the earth (plants), from moisture (microbes), from the womb (mammals), and from an egg (birds and reptiles). This shows the Grace-Light as the single, universal source for every form of life.

translit: ūrvaṉa paṟappaṉa vuṟuvaṉa naṭappaṉa ārvuṟa vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which lovingly fashioned those that crawl, those that fly, those that abide and those that walk.
commentary: The Grace-Light creates all living things with love and care. This verse categorizes beings by how they move through the world, but the key idea is that creation is an act of divine affection, not a cold or mechanical process.

translit: acaivila vacaivuḷa vāruyirt tiraḷpala acalaṟa vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which flawlessly fashions the many multitudes of precious lives, both motionless and mobile.
commentary: All of existence, from motionless beings like plants and stones to mobile ones like animals, is created perfectly by the Grace-Light. By dividing all of life into these two simple groups, Vallalar shows the comprehensive and flawless nature of the divine creative power.

translit: aṟivoru vakaimuta laivakai yaṟuvakai aṟitara vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which establishes the levels of consciousness, from one sense up to five and six, so that beings may perceive.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the source of physical form and of consciousness itself. It establishes the different levels of awareness, traditionally classified by the number of senses a being possesses, from one-sensed plants to six-sensed humans (five senses plus intellect). This divine ordering allows each creature to perceive the world according to its capacity.

translit: vevvē ṟiyaloṭu vevvēṟu payaṉuṟa avvā ṟamaitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you established things with distinct natures to yield distinct results.
commentary: The world is not chaotic; it operates on a principle of cause and effect established by the divine light. Every thing, quality, and action has its own distinct nature and produces a corresponding result, creating an ordered and predictable universe.

translit: cittira vicittira ciruṭṭikaḷ palapala attakai vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you arranged the many, many marvelous and varied creations.
commentary: This is a moment of pure wonder at the sheer beauty and endless variety of the world. All of this magnificent diversity, from the smallest to the largest, originates from the singular, creative intelligence of the divine light.

translit: peṇṇiṉuḷ ḷāṇu māṇiṉuṭ peṇṇum aṇṇuṟa vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you fittingly established the masculine within the feminine and the feminine within the masculine.
commentary: Gender is not a rigid binary but a fluid blend. The divine light has placed what we consider masculine qualities within the feminine form, and feminine qualities within the masculine, suggesting an inner wholeness and balance in every person.

translit: peṇṇiṉuṇ mūṉṟu māṇiṉuḷ ḷiraṇṭum aṇṇuṟa vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you fittingly established the three within the feminine and the two within the masculine.
commentary: The verb is வகுத்த (vakutta), to apportion: to take a whole and divide it into allotted shares. The locative is உள் (uḷ), within. The Vast Grace-Light divides an interior reality, granting the female three shares of it against the male's two.

Read alongside the next couplet, a progression appears. The counts rise to four and three, the verb shifts to அமைத்த (amaitta, to set in place), and the locative changes to இடை (iṭai, among). Across both, the defining feature is a precise asymmetry: the female consistently carries exactly one share more than the male, whatever is being measured.

The three within the female is attested. The Upadesa Kurippukal names three stations where Bindu resides in the female body , பெண்களுக்குப் பிந்து இருக்கிற ஸ்தானம் மூன்று: வாய், மார்பு, ஸ்தனத்தின் கீழ் , the mouth, the chest, below the breasts. The two within the male has no counterpart in any text that survives to us. Vallalar states the proportion and leaves half of it unnamed, allowing the blueprint itself to be the teaching. The human body is revealed not as an accident of matter but as a closely calibrated vessel, made to be conserved, purified, and eventually transmuted.

This structural asymmetry is not a hierarchy of rank between female and male. In Suddha Sanmarkkam there is no higher soul and no lower one; all beings share a supreme and equal kinship (Anma Neya Orumaipadu). A greater share of light in one form is a fact of construction, a specification for the alchemical furnace, and nothing more.

translit: peṇṇiṭai nāṉku māṇiṭai mūṉṟum aṇṇuṟa vamaitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you fittingly established the four within the feminine and the three within the masculine.
commentary: Two words shift from the previous couplet. The verb becomes அமைத்த (amaitta), to arrange or set in place. The locative becomes இடை (iṭai), among or at. Where 353 apportioned the shares, this couplet positions them.
Here the counts are directly attested. The Upadesa Kurippukal gives this four-to-three proportion twice in explicit terms:

The light of Bindu. ஆணிடத்தில் பிந்து விளக்கம் மூன்று பங்கும், பெண்ணிடத்தில் பிந்து விளக்கம் நான்கு பங்கும் , three parts of Bindu-illumination in the male, four in the female. Vallalar applies this to a single observable fact: where the illumination is dense, coarse body hair does not grow. He calls its prominence தத்துவ ஆபாசம், a distortion at the level of the constructed principles.

The stations of vital essence. Three centres in the male body (the brain within the skull, the navel, the underside of the lingam) and four in the female (the brain, below the breasts, the navel, the private parts).

The proportion recurs once more in a form that resists any reading of rank. Within the female sac, a cluster of three beads lies on the right and four on the left. Should the semen meet the three, a male child is born; should it meet the four, a female. Both numbers are held in one body, and each generates the other kind. Neither share is anyone's property, and neither builds alone.

This is why Vallalar refused to let his path be read as devotion only. A body assembled to measure is a body that can be worked on. The same passage that counts the stations gives the instruction for keeping them: தேகத்தைத் திறந்து வைத்திருத்தல் ஆகாது; சத்துக் காய்ந்து போம் , the body must not be left exposed, or the essence dries away. Conserve the vital essence, steady the breath, keep the hand free of killing and the plate free of flesh, and the architecture that assembles a mortal frame will assemble a deathless one. The compassion is not a moral addition to the physiology. It is the physiology.

translit: peṇṇiya lāṇu māṇiyaṟ peṇṇum aṇṇuṟa vamaitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which intimately fashioned the male of feminine nature and the female of masculine nature.
commentary: The Divine Light is the source of human diversity, creating people who embody a blend of gender characteristics. Long before modern ideas on this topic, Vallalar saw this spectrum not as an anomaly, but as an intimate and intentional act of creation.

translit: peṇṭiṟal puṟattu māṇṭiṟa lakattum aṇṭuṟa vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which arranged for female power to be external and male power internal.
commentary: The creative force is described as arranging a balance between male and female energies. Feminine power is associated here with outward expression and manifest action, while masculine power is seen as an inner, foundational potential.

translit: peṇṇiyaṉ maṉamu māṇiya laṟivum aṇṇuṟa vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which intimately arranged the mind of feminine nature and the intellect of masculine nature.
commentary: The divinely ordered complementarity continues. It associates the fluid, multifaceted nature of the mind with the feminine principle, and the discerning, focused quality of the intellect with the masculine.

translit: taṉittaṉi vaṭiviṉun takkavāṇ peṇṇiyal aṉaittuṟa vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which arranged for all fitting masculine and feminine qualities to be present in each and every form.
commentary: The distinctions made in previous verses are resolved with a profound insight: every individual being contains a blend of all these masculine and feminine qualities. The Divine Light did not create rigid categories, but a spectrum of traits present in everyone.

translit: uṉaṟkaru muyiruḷa vuṭaluḷa vulakuḷa vaṉaittaiyum vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which created everything that exists: lives difficult to conceive, bodies, and worlds.
commentary: The poem’s focus now expands from human qualities to the entire cosmos. The Vast Grace-Light is presented as the ultimate source of everything, including the countless forms of life beyond our comprehension, the physical bodies they inhabit, and the very worlds they live on.

translit: ōvuṟā veḻuvakai yuyirmuta laṉaittum āvakai vakutta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which ordained the ways of being for all, beginning with the seven unceasing types of life.
commentary: All of creation is ordered into distinct categories, and this order itself is an expression of the Grace-Light. The "seven types of life" refers to a traditional classification system encompassing all beings, from gods to plants, showing that divine intelligence is behind the very structure of the living world.

translit: paikaḷiṉ muṭṭaiyiṟ pāriṉil vērviṉil aipeṟa vamaitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which marvelously created beings to emerge from wombs, from eggs, from the earth, and from moisture.
commentary: The variety in how life begins is itself a marvel of the Grace-Light's creation. This verse refers to the four traditional categories of birth: from the womb, from the egg, from the earth (like plants sprouting), and from moisture, showing that the divine hand is present in every method of generation.

translit: tāykarup paiyiṉuṭ ṭaṅkiya vuyirkaḷai āyvuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously and meticulously protects the lives that reside within the mother's womb.
commentary: The Grace-Light is not a remote creator but an intimate protector, actively and carefully nurturing life in its most vulnerable state. Its grace extends even to the unborn, watching over their development within the womb.

translit: muṭṭaivāyp payilu muḻuvuyirt tiraḷkaḷai aṭṭamē kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously and closely protects the multitudes of complete lives developing within the egg.
commentary: Just as it protects life in the womb, the Grace-Light extends its close, personal protection to all beings developing inside eggs. This care is universal, recognizing the sanctity of every individual life, even before it has hatched.

translit: nilampeṟu muyirvakai nīḷkuḻu vaṉaittum alampeṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously protects all the vast multitudes of life that come from the earth, causing them to flourish.
commentary: The protective grace of the divine light extends to the entire plant kingdom and all other life born from the earth. It is the force that creates them and actively sustains them, ensuring that they thrive and flourish.

translit: vērvuṟa vutitta mikumuyirt tiraḷkaḷai ārvuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Supreme Grace-Light that lovingly protects the abundant multitudes of lives born from sweat.
commentary: Beings "born from sweat" is an ancient class for micro-life such as bacteria, insects and microbes. By including them, Vallalar makes a clear point: absolutely no living thing, however small or seemingly insignificant, is outside the circle of divine care.

translit: uṭaluṟu piṇiyā luyiruṭal keṭāvakai aṭaluṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Supreme Grace-Light that powerfully protects, preventing life and body from being destroyed by diseases that afflict the body.
commentary: Divine grace is more than a high-minded spiritual concept; it is directly concerned with the health of the body. Here, the Supreme Grace-Light is a power that actively works to protect living beings from the physical destruction caused by illness and our ignorance.

translit: cicumutaṟ paruvac ceyalkaḷi ṉuyirkaḷai acaivaṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Supreme Grace-Light that steadfastly protects beings through the activities of life's stages, from infancy onward.
commentary: The protection of the Grace-Light is constant throughout a creature's entire lifespan. It is present in the vulnerability of infancy, the challenges of youth, and the changes of adulthood, providing steadfast support at every stage.

translit: uyiruṟu muṭalaiyu muṭaluṟu muyiraiyum ayarvaṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Supreme Grace-Light that tirelessly protects the body that holds life and the life that is in the body.
commentary: Life and the body that holds it are a sacred unity. The divine cares for both together, recognizing that one cannot be separated from the other. This protection is described as tireless, an eternal and unfailing aspect of God's nature.

translit: pāṭuṟu mavattaikaḷ palaviṉu muyirkaḷai āṭuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Supreme Grace-Light that protects beings through their many painful states of experience, enabling them to flourish.
commentary: Even in moments of great suffering or confusing states of mind (avattaikaḷ), the divine is present. This protection does more than help one endure pain; it provides the energy to transform that experience into growth and vitality.

translit: muccuṭa rātiyā leccaka vuyiraiyum accaṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously protects all lives in every world, removing their fear, through the three primary lights and more.
commentary: The "three primary lights" (muccuṭar) are the sun, the moon, and fire. Vallalar sees these fundamental sources of light and energy not as mere physical phenomena, but as expressions of the Grace-Light's power, actively working to sustain all beings and free them from fear.

translit: vāṉmukiṟ cattiyāṉ maḻaipoḻi vittuyir āṉaṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously protects life for its well-being, causing rain to pour by the power of the sky's clouds.
commentary: Natural phenomena like rain are not random or impersonal events. Vallalar understands them as the deliberate, compassionate actions of the Divine, manifesting through its specific power (satti) in the clouds to sustain and nourish all life.

translit: iṉpuṟu cattiyā leḻiṉmaḻai poḻivit taṉpuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously protects with love, causing beautiful rain to pour by the power that brings joy.
commentary: Here, the power (satti) that causes rain is identified with the power that creates joy. The life-giving rain is a direct expression of divine love, a gift meant to bring delight and well-being to the world.

translit: eṇṇiyaṟ cattiyā lellā vulakiṉum aṇṇuyir kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously protects the lives in every world by the power of divine thought.
commentary: The existence and protection of all worlds and the beings within them are sustained by the "power of divine thought." Everything is held in existence by a conscious, intentional divine will, a power (satti) that is itself a form of supreme intelligence.

translit: aṇṭap puṟappuṟa vamutam poḻintuyir aṇṭuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which showers nectar in the regions beyond the beyond of the cosmos, graciously protecting life so that it may draw near.
commentary: The "nectar" (amutam) is the ambrosia of immortality and divine bliss. This verse extends the reach of grace beyond the physical world to the highest spiritual planes, the "regions beyond the beyond." Even there, the Grace-Light actively nourishes souls, helping them complete their journey toward union with God.

translit: tēvarai yellān tikaḻpuṟa vamutaḷit tāvakai kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi gives the shining outer nectar and graciously protects all the celestial beings.
commentary: The divine light provides specific kinds of spiritual nourishment for different beings. The celestial gods (tēvar) are sustained by a 'shining outer nectar' (tikaḻ puṟa amutam), a form of grace suited to their level of existence. This implies a subtle hierarchy of grace, with other, deeper forms available to different souls.

translit: akappuṟa vamutaḷit taivarā tikaḷai akappaṭak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi gives the inner-outer nectar and graciously protects by bringing the five senses and their companions under control.
commentary: A different kind of grace, the 'inner-outer nectar' (akappuṟa amutam), helps beings who are struggling with their five senses. This grace works both internally and externally to bring the senses and their associated impulses under control. Here, grace is an active force that helps one achieve the self-mastery needed for spiritual progress.

translit: tarumaka vamutāṟ catticat tarkaḷai aruḷiṉiṟ kākku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi protects the Saktis and Saktas in grace through the inner nectar it bestows.
commentary: The deepest form of grace, the 'inner nectar' (akam amutam), is reserved for the most advanced spiritual beings. It sustains the Saktis and Saktas (divine powers and highly devoted souls), protecting them from within. This completes a progression of grace, from outer to inner-outer, and finally to this purely internal experience for those closest to the divine.

translit: kālamu niyatiyuṅ kāṭṭiyev vuyiraiyum āluṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi reveals time and cosmic order, and graciously protects every being with loving care.
commentary: The divine light establishes the fundamental structures of reality: time (kālam) and cosmic law (niyati). This ordering of the universe is not impersonal; the same light lovingly protects every being within that system. Cosmic law is not a cold, mechanical force, but an expression of divine care and affection for all life.

translit: viccaiyai yiccaiyai viḷaivit tuyirkaḷai accaṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi causes knowledge and desire to arise in beings and graciously protects them, freeing them from fear.
commentary: The fundamental drives that shape our lives, knowledge (viccai) and desire (icchai), are themselves sparked by the divine light. Instead of being seen as worldly traps, they are presented here as divine tools given to us for our own growth. By kindling these impulses, the light guides our evolution and ultimately frees us from fear.

translit: pōkamuṅ kaḷippum poruntuvit tuyirkaḷai ākamuṭ kākku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, uniting souls with enjoyment and delight, protects them within their bodies.
commentary: Enjoyment (pōkam) and worldly delight are not always obstacles to spiritual life, but are themselves gifts of the Grace-Light. The physical body is the sacred place where the soul is lovingly protected and allowed to experience these joys.

translit: kalaiyaṟi vaḷittuk kaḷippiṉi luyirelām alaivaṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, bestowing knowledge of the arts, graciously protects all souls in delight, keeping them from turmoil.
commentary: The knowledge of arts and sciences (kalai aṟivu) is a specific gift from the Grace-Light, meant to bring joy and calm the mind. Creativity and culture are not mere human pastimes, but divine means of protecting the soul from inner turmoil.

translit: viṭaya nikaḻcciyāṉ mikumuyi raṉaittaiyum aṭaivuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, through the events of sensory experience, graciously protects all the many souls in an orderly way.
commentary: The endless stream of sensory perceptions that make up our daily lives is not random. The Grace-Light organizes these experiences (viṭaya nikḻcci) in a meaningful order, using them as a way to guide and protect each soul on its path.

translit: tuṉpaḷit tāṅkē cukamaḷit tuyirkaḷai aṉpuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, giving suffering and then pleasure in that very place, graciously protects souls with love.
commentary: Suffering (tuṉpam) and pleasure (sukam) are two sides of the same divine, loving process. The Grace-Light gives us both, often in the same situation, as a way to teach and guide our growth, transforming pain from a meaningless affliction into a purposeful event.

translit: karaṇēn tiyattāṟ kaḷippuṟa vuyirkaḷai araṇērn taḷittaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, providing a fortress of protection, graciously enables souls to delight through their inner faculties and outer senses.
commentary: Our inner faculties (karaṇam) and outer senses (intiyam) are not traps that lead us astray. The Grace-Light provides them as a protective fortress (araṇ), tools that allow us to experience the world with security and delight.

translit: ettakai yevvuyi reṇṇiṉa vavvuyirk kattakai yaḷittaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: In whatever way beings conceive, Arutperunjothi graciously provides to those beings in that very same way.
commentary: The divine Grace-Light meets every being on its own terms. Whatever concept of God a soul holds, Grace responds in that very form, providing what is needed in a way that the soul can understand and receive.

translit: eppaṭi yevvuyi reṇṇiṉa vavvuyirk kappaṭi yaḷittaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: However beings conceive, Arutperunjothi graciously provides to those beings in that very same way.
commentary: The previous couplet is reinforced. The divine responds to the content of our belief and to the manner in which we believe. The way a soul thinks and feels about God determines the way it receives a response.

translit: ēṅkā tuyirttira ḷeṅkeṅ kiruntaṉa āṅkāṅ kaḷittaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Wherever the multitudes of beings exist, Arutperunjothi graciously provides for them in those very places, so they do not languish.
commentary: Divine grace is not confined to a holy place or a chosen few. It is everywhere, actively providing for all beings in their specific locations and circumstances so that none are left abandoned or in want.

translit: colluṟu macuttat tolluyirk kavvakai allaliṟ kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: For the ancient souls in the state called asuddham, Arutperunjothi graciously protects them from suffering in a manner befitting them.
commentary: Even souls in the state of asuddham (impurity), a condition of deep spiritual ignorance, are not abandoned. The Grace-Light offers a form of protection specifically suited to their limited state, preventing them from being completely overcome by suffering.

translit: cuttamu macuttamun tōyuyirk kirumaiyiṉ attakai kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: For the souls connected to both suddham and asuddham, Arutperunjothi graciously protects them in a manner fitting their dual nature.
commentary: Most beings exist in a mixed state, touched by both suddham (purity, clarity) and asuddham (impurity, ignorance). For these souls, the Grace-Light provides a tailored form of protection that addresses this inner duality, helping them navigate the path between the two.

translit: vāyntiṭuñ cutta vakaiyuyirk korumaiyiṉ āyntuṟak kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which discerningly and graciously protects, in oneness, the souls of the pure kind.
commentary: For souls who have reached a state of purity, the Grace-Light's protection focuses on preserving their oneness. As beings become purer, their sense of separation dissolves into a collective unity, a state which divine grace actively discerns and sustains.

translit: evaiyelā mevaiyelā mīṇṭiṉa vīṇṭiṉa avaiyelāṅ kāttaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which graciously protects absolutely everything that has come to be and gathered here.
commentary: The protection of the Grace-Light is absolute and all-encompassing. It extends to every single thing that has come into existence, without any exception whatsoever.

translit: aṇṭat turicaiyu makilat turicaiyum aṇṭaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which utterly subdues the impurity of the cosmos and the defilement of the universe.
commentary: The Grace-Light’s purifying power works on a cosmic scale. It is capable of subduing the deep-seated defilements within a person and within the entire universe.

translit: piṇṭat turicaiyum pēruyirt turicaiyum aṇṭaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which utterly subdues the impurity of the physical body and the defilement of the great soul.
commentary: The same grace that purifies the cosmos also works within the individual. It cleanses the impurities of the physical body and the taints that cling to the soul, showing that one power purifies both the personal and the universal.

translit: uyiruṟu māyaiyi ṉuṟuviri vaṉaittum ayiraṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which flawlessly subdues all potent expansions of the Māyā that afflict the soul.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the ultimate remedy for delusion. It flawlessly overcomes all the intricate workings of Māyā, the cosmic power of illusion that creates a false sense of reality and keeps the soul entangled.

translit: uyiruṟu miruviṉai yuṟuviri vaṉaittum ayarvaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you untiringly subdue all the ramifications arising from the two karmas that affect the soul.
commentary: The 'two karmas' (iruvinai) are the consequences of our good and bad actions. Punnyam is good karma and Papam is bad karma In many Indian traditions, both bind the soul to the cycle of rebirth. Grace is the power that can erase this accumulated debt, freeing the soul from the endless loop of cause and effect.

translit: kāmap puṭaippuyir kaṇṭoṭa rāvakai āmaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you completely subdue the swelling of lust so that it does not pursue the soul, utterly rooting it out.
commentary: The Grace-Light does more than help one manage desire; it removes it completely. The verse describes lust (kāmam) as a 'swelling,' a powerful affliction, which grace dissolves so thoroughly that it can no longer even pursue the soul.

translit: poṅkuṟu vekuḷip puṭaippuka ḷellām aṅkaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you subdue all the swellings of surging anger, destroying them on the spot.
commentary: Like lust, anger (vekuḷi) is a destructive force that swells up within us. The Grace-Light is presented as an immediate remedy that destroys anger the moment it appears, extinguishing it on the spot.

translit: matampurai mōkamu maṟṟavu māṅkāṅ katampeṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you subdue pride, delusion, and other such things, bringing them to an end wherever they arise.
commentary: The work of grace extends to the core attitudes of the ego. It dissolves pride (matam), which creates a false sense of self, and delusion (mōkam), which causes us to be infatuated with things that are unreal or fleeting.

translit: vaṭuvuṟu macutta vātaṉai yaṉaittaiyum aṭarpaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you subdue all the blemishing, impure latent tendencies, destroying their dense hold.
commentary: The deepest and most stubborn obstacles to spiritual progress are our unconscious habits and tendencies, called vātanai. These are the imprints left by past actions that cause us to react in old, conditioned ways. The Grace-Light penetrates this deep level of the self, erasing these patterns and enabling true freedom.

translit: cuttamu macuttamun tōyntavā taṉaikaḷai attakai yaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi completely subdues the latent tendencies steeped in both purity and impurity.
commentary: Most spiritual paths teach us to overcome impurity and cultivate purity. Vallalar says that the Grace-Light, Arutperunjothi, dissolves both. Even "good" karma or attachment to being virtuous is a bond that must be broken to achieve a state beyond all duality. True freedom means being liberated from the effects of both good and bad actions.

translit: nālvayiṟ ṟuricum naṇṇuyi rātiyil ālaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi utterly uproots and quells the fourfold impurities that have been with the soul from its origin.
commentary: The impurities that bind the soul are not superficial; they have been with it from the very beginning. They are usually named ego (āṇavam), illusion (māyai), past actions (karmam) and the veiling power (tirōtāyi). The Grace-Light reaches back to the soul's origin and erases even these primordial stains.

translit: nālvayiṟ paṭaippu nālvayiṟ kāppum ālaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi utterly uproots and quells the fourfold creation and the fourfold preservation.
commentary: The power of the Grace-Light extends beyond the individual soul to the cosmos itself. It can dissolve the very processes of creation and preservation that structure our universe, pointing to a state of being that transcends all manifested reality.

translit: mūviṭat tirumaiyiṉ muṉṉiya toḻiṟkaril āviṭat taṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi subdues, right in their sphere of action, the agents who perform the dual functions across the three realms.
commentary: The universe is governed by cosmic forces that operate in pairs, like creation and destruction or pleasure and pain. Vallalar states that the Grace-Light is the supreme authority that controls even these governing powers across all realms of existence.

translit: mūviṭa mummaiyiṉ muṉṉiya toḻiṟkaril āviṭa maṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi subdues, right in their sphere of action, the agents who perform the triple functions across the three realms.
commentary: The Grace-Light is superior to the great gods of creation, preservation, and destruction. It is the ultimate source from which even these divine beings draw their power, and it can absorb their functions back into itself. For Vallalar, the formless Grace-Light is the absolute and final reality.

translit: tattuvac cēṭṭaiyun tattuvat turicum attakai yaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you suppress the agitations and impurities of the tattvas.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the power that can pacify the fundamental building blocks of reality, the tattvas. When these principles are agitated, they create inner turmoil and bondage, but the Light brings them to a state of stillness and purity.

translit: cuttamā nilaiyiṟ cūḻuṟu virivai attakai yaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you suppress the encompassing expansion that arises from the state of pure maya.
commentary: Maya is the cosmic power of illusion that creates the appearance of a diverse universe. Even in its purest, most subtle form, it leads to an endless expansion of worlds that distract the soul. The Grace-Light has the power to quiet this expansive energy, revealing the single reality behind the many forms.

translit: karaiviṉmā māyaik karumperun tiraiyāl araicatu maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you hide the Sovereign with the great black screen of indissoluble, immense maya.
commentary: Here Vallalar introduces a key idea: reality is hidden from us by screens or veils. The first and densest of these is the "great black screen" of maya, the fundamental cosmic illusion. Paradoxically, the Grace-Light itself places this veil, hiding God (the Sovereign) from the soul's direct perception.

translit: pēruṟu nīlap peruntirai yataṉāl āruyir maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you hide the precious soul with the vast, great blue screen.
commentary: After the black screen that hides God, a "great blue screen" hides the soul from itself. This veil prevents the soul from realizing its own inherent light and divine nature.

translit: paccait tiraiyāṟ paraveḷi yataṉai accuṟa maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, you formidably hide the supreme expanse with the green screen.
commentary: The third veil is a "green screen," which conceals the "supreme expanse" (paraveḷi). This screen blocks the soul's access to the vast spiritual space where higher divine powers and subtle energies operate.

translit: cemmait tiraiyāṟ cittuṟu veḷiyai ammaiyiṉ maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, with the red screen, conceals the space of consciousness in that very state.
commentary: The red screen conceals the cittu veḷi, the space of pure consciousness. This veil operates at the level of awareness itself, obscuring the pristine, unmodified consciousness that is the source of all thought and perception.

translit: poṉmait tiraiyāṟ poruḷuṟu veḷiyai aṉmaiyiṉ maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, with the golden screen, conceals the space of substance in otherness.
commentary: A golden screen obscures the poruḷ veḷi, the space of ultimate substance or truth. This veil creates the illusion of "otherness," making us perceive the world as a collection of separate objects rather than a unified reality.

translit: veṇmait tiraiyāṉ meyppati veḷiyai aṇmaiyiṉ maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, with the white screen, conceals the space of the True Abode in nearness.
commentary: Even the final destination, the True Abode (meyppati), is concealed by a white screen. Paradoxically, this veil makes what is nearest to us seem distant, suggesting the final barrier to God is the most subtle one.

translit: kalapput tiraiyāṟ karutaṉu pavaṅkaḷai alappuṟa maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, with the screen of mixed colors, conceals conceived experiences, causing great distress.
commentary: A screen of mixed colors represents the confusion of our own minds. It jumbles our thoughts and experiences, preventing clear perception and causing the mental and emotional distress of ordinary life.

translit: viṭaya nilaikaḷai vevvēṟu tiraikaḷāl aṭarpuṟa maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, with various different screens, densely conceals the states of sensory objects.
commentary: In sum, the effect of all the veils: The world we perceive through our senses (viṭaya nilai) is not reality itself, but a version densely filtered and obscured by these various screens.

translit: tattuva nilaikaḷait taṉittaṉit tiraiyāl attiṟa maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which conceals the levels of the tattvas with their own separate veils.
commentary: Even the fundamental principles of existence, the tattvas, are concealed by their own specific veils. Each layer of reality has its own screen that hides it from our direct perception.

translit: tiraimaṟaip pellān tīrttāṅ kāṅkē aracuṟak kāṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which removes all the concealments of the veils and, right then and there, reveals the reigning truth.
commentary: The same Divine Light that sets up all these veils is also the only power that can remove them. When it does, the truth is revealed immediately, without any delay or intermediary.

translit: tōṟṟamā māyait toṭarpaṟut taruḷi ṉāṟṟalaik kāṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which severs the connection to the maya of appearances and shows the power of Grace.
commentary: The Divine Light severs our attachment to māyā, the cosmic illusion that generates the world of appearances. Once freed from this illusion, we can directly perceive the power of Grace.

translit: cuttamā māyait toṭarpaṟut taruḷai attakai kāṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which severs the connection to suddha maya and reveals Grace in its true nature.
commentary: Beyond the ordinary illusion of the physical world, there is a subtler formative power called suddha māyā, or "pure illusion," which is the very blueprint of creation. The Divine Light severs our connection even to this, revealing Grace in its ultimate, unconditioned nature.

translit: eṉaittā ṇavamuta lellān tavirttē aṉukkira kampuri yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which removes everything, beginning with āṇavam, and bestows its anugraham.
commentary: The most fundamental veil is āṇavam, the deep-seated sense of being a separate "I". The Divine Light removes this core principle of ego and everything associated with it, bestowing its ultimate blessing, which is called anugraham (divine grace).

translit: viṭaya maṟaippelām viṭuvit tuyirkaḷai aṭaivuṟat teruṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi releases souls from all concealments caused by worldly phenomena and enlightens them fittingly.
commentary: The constant stream of worldly experiences and sense objects, called viṭayam, can distract and confuse us, hiding the truth. The Grace-Light frees souls from this concealment, giving them the precise clarity they need.

translit: corupa maṟaippelān tolaippit tuyirkaḷai aruḷiṉiṟ ṟeruṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi destroys all concealments of the soul's true form and enlightens them through grace.
commentary: Our true self, the soul's essential form (sorupam), is hidden beneath layers of conditioning and ignorance. The Grace-Light destroys these veils and uses Grace itself as the tool of enlightenment.

translit: maṟaippiṉ maṟantaṉa varuvit tāṅkē aṟattoṭu teruṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi brings back what was forgotten due to concealment and, right then and there, enlightens with righteousness.
commentary: Spiritual awakening is presented here as an act of remembering. The Grace-Light brings back the divine truth we have forgotten. This realization is more than a thought; it happens instantly and brings with it an understanding of aṟam, or righteous living.

translit: evvakai yuyirkaḷu miṉpuṟa vāṅkē avvakai teruṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi enlightens all kinds of souls in such a way that they experience bliss.
commentary: The Grace-Light’s guidance is not a rigid system, but is uniquely tailored to each soul. It provides whatever form of enlightenment is needed to bring that specific being to a state of bliss.

translit: kaṭavuḷar maṟaippaik kaṭintavark kiṉpam aṭaiyuṟat teruṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi removes the concealment caused by the gods and enlightens those souls so they attain bliss.
commentary: It seems that those lower gods may exercise obscuring power on the spiritual practitioner. The Grace-Light helps the soul see beyond these specific divine forms, removing this subtle "concealment by the gods" so that unmediated bliss can be attained.

translit: cattikaṇ maṟaippait tavirttavark kiṉpam attuṟat teruṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which enlightens with perfect bliss those who have removed the veiling of the Saktis.
commentary: The path requires moving beyond attachment to even the highest divine forces, here named as the Saktis (the great goddesses or personified feminine energies of the cosmos). The Grace-Light reveals the ultimate reality that lies beyond them, granting perfect bliss to those who are no longer limited by these powerful forms.

translit: cattarkaṇ maṟaippait tavirttavark kiṉpam attakai teruṭṭum aruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which enlightens with that same quality of bliss those who have removed the veiling of the Saktars.
commentary: Just as with the feminine powers, the masculine divine powers, or Saktars, can also become a spiritual limitation if they are seen as the final goal. The Grace-Light enables the soul to transcend these cosmic lords and experience the same supreme bliss, which comes from knowing the reality that is their source.

translit: paṭaikkun talaivarkaḷ paṟpala kōṭiyai aṭaippuṟap paṭaikkum aruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which creates and contains within Itself many tens of millions of creator-lords.
commentary: The Grace-Light is the ultimate source of creation itself. Even the millions of beings who are themselves lords of creation are brought into being by, and exist within, this one Vast Grace-Light.

translit: kākkun talaivarkaḷ kaṇakkilpal kōṭiyai ākkuṟak kākku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which establishes and protects the countless tens of millions of lords of preservation.
commentary: All divine beings responsible for sustaining and preserving the cosmos are themselves sustained by the Grace-Light. It is the power that establishes these "lords of preservation" and allows them to perform their cosmic function.

translit: aṭakkun talaivarka ḷaḷavilar tammaiyum aṭarppaṟa vaṭakku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which effortlessly subdues the innumerable lords of dissolution.
commentary: The Grace-Light also holds supreme authority over the forces of cosmic dissolution. The countless lords who govern endings and destruction are themselves effortlessly governed by the Grace-Light, which contains and controls all cosmic functions.

translit: maṟaikkun talaivarkaḷ vakaipala kōṭiyai aṟattoṭu maṟaikku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which utterly obscures the many crores of leaders who conceal the truth.
commentary: The Divine Light completely overpowers all forces of illusion that conceal the ultimate truth from souls. In its presence, all that obscures reality simply dissolves.

translit: teruṭṭun talaivarkaḷ cērpala kōṭiyai aruṭṭiṟan teruṭṭu maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which, by the power of Grace, enlightens the many crores of leaders who offer clarification.
commentary: Just as Arutperunjothi neutralizes illusion, it is also the source of all revelation. Even the divine beings whose role is to guide souls toward truth receive their power to enlighten from the Grace-Light alone.

translit: aintoḻi lāticey yaivarā tikaḷai aintoḻi lāticey yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which makes the Five Lords and the others, who perform the five functions and more, perform those functions.
commentary: The five cosmic functions (aintoḻil: creation, preservation, dissolution, veiling and grace) are carried out by the Five Lords, but not by their own power. Arutperunjothi, the Vast Grace-Light, directs them and makes them act.

translit: iṟantava rellā meḻuntiṭa vulakil aṟantalai yaḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which bestowed the highest form of justice on the world, enabling all the dead to rise.
commentary: The supreme act of justice performed by the Grace-Light is to overturn death itself. Vallalar presents physical resurrection as a possibility, suggesting not to cremate the dead but bury them.

translit: cettava rellāñ cirittāṅ keḻutiṟal attakai kāṭṭiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, which revealed such a wonder: the power for all who died to rise up laughing.
commentary: The resurrection enabled by Arutperunjothi is not a grim or solemn affair. Those who rise from death do so with laughter, expressing the sheer joy and triumph of life’s ultimate victory over mortality.

translit: iṟantava reḻukaveṉ ṟeṇṇiyāṅ keḻuppiṭa aṟantuṇai yeṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi grants me righteousness as my support, enabling me to think "Let the dead arise" and to raise them up.
commentary: The divine power to resurrect the dead is something God does and a power that can be given to a human being. Vallalar states that Grace has granted him the ability to raise the dead simply by thinking it, with righteousness (aṟam) as his foundation and support.

translit: cettava reḻukeṉac ceppiyāṅ keḻuppiṭa attiṟa leṉakkaru ḷaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi grants me that very power to command "Let the dead arise" and to raise them up.
commentary: Here, the power given to Vallalar becomes even more direct. He doesn't just need to think it; he can now command the dead to rise with his words. This verse shows a progression where the divine power of grace becomes fully active and present in his own being.

translit: cittelām valla tiṟalaḷit teṉakkē attaṉeṉ ṟōṅku maruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Arutperunjothi, soaring as my Father, has granted me the power that can accomplish all siddhis.
commentary: The power given by grace is not limited to resurrection; it is the capacity to achieve all siddhis, or supernatural powers. Vallalar describes the source of this ability, Arutperunjothi, with great intimacy as his own Father, who grants him this unlimited potential.

translit: oṉṟati raṇṭatu voṉṟiṉi raṇṭatu oṉṟiṉu ḷoṉṟatu voṉṟeṉu moṉṟē
translation: It is One. It is Two. It is the Two in the One. It is the One within the One. It is the very One called "One".
commentary: Numbers describe the paradoxical nature of the ultimate reality. It is the absolute One, yet it also appears as Two (like God and soul, or spirit and matter). It is both at once, and it is also beyond any of these descriptions. This is not a logical puzzle but a mystical expression of a truth that contains all possibilities.

translit: oṉṟala raṇṭala voṉṟiṉi raṇṭala oṉṟiṉu ḷoṉṟala voṉṟeṉu moṉṟē
translation: It is not One. It is not Two. It is not the Two in the One. It is not the One within the One. It is the very One called "One".
commentary: After describing what the ultimate reality is, Vallalar now describes what it is not. It is not one, not two, and not any combination of these concepts. This is a classic mystical teaching: the Divine is beyond all human categories and language. By saying what it is and then what it is not, he points toward a truth that can only be experienced, not defined.

translit: oṉṟiṉi loṉṟuḷa voṉṟiṉi loṉṟila oṉṟaṟa voṉṟiya voṉṟeṉu moṉṟē
translation: The One that is within another, the One that is not within another, the One that has merged to become indivisibly one, the very One called the One.
commentary: God is described as both dwelling within creation and existing entirely beyond it. This captures the simultaneous immanence and transcendence of the divine. The verse then points to the spiritual goal: the soul merges with God so completely that all separation disappears, becoming "indivisibly one."

translit: kaḷaṅkanīt tulakaṅ kaḷippuṟa meynneṟi viḷaṅkaveṉ ṉuḷḷē viḷaṅkumeyp poruḷē
translation: You are the True Substance, shining within me to banish imperfection, make the world rejoice, and illuminate the True Path.
commentary: The focus shifts from abstract ideas to a direct, personal experience of God. The divine is not a distant concept but a "True Substance" (meyp poruḷ) that shines within the individual. This inner presence has a powerful purpose: to purify the self, bring joy to the world, and light up the path to truth.

translit: mūviru nilaiyiṉ muṭinaṭu muṭimēl ōvaṟa viḷaṅku morumaimeyp poruḷē
translation: O singular True Substance, you shine without end at the crown, the center of the crown, and above the crown of the six-fold state.
commentary: The divine is experienced as a radiant light at the highest point of human consciousness. In the language of inner yoga, the "six-fold state" refers to the primary energy centers of the body. Vallalar locates the experience of God at the "crown," the highest of these centers, and even beyond it, as a constant, unending source of light.

translit: eḻunilai micaiyē yiṉpuru vāki vaḻunilai nīkki vayaṅkumeyp poruḷē
translation: O shining True Substance, you become a form of bliss above the seven levels, removing the state of error.
commentary: Reaching the highest spiritual planes brings about a profound transformation. Above the "seven levels" of consciousness, the divine is experienced as light and as pure bliss. This experience of bliss is what removes all delusion and error, grounding the soul in unshakeable truth.

translit: navanilai micaiyē naṭuvuṟu naṭuvē civamaya mākit tikaḻntameyp poruḷē
translation: O True Substance, you shine as pure Sivam in the very center of the center, above the nine levels.
commentary: Here is the absolute peak of spiritual realization. Beyond the "nine levels" of consciousness, in the innermost core of being, God is revealed as Sivamayam, meaning completely filled with Sivam. In this context, Sivam means the formless, ultimate, and purely auspicious reality, the final state of truth and grace.

translit: ēkā tacanilai yātati ṉaṭuvē ēkā taṉamicai yiruntameyp poruḷē
translation: O True Substance, seated on the singular throne in the center of the eleventh state.
commentary: The ascent through inner states of being continues. Here, in the eleventh stage, the divine reality is depicted as a sovereign presence, alone on a throne at the very center.

translit: tiraiyō tacanilai civaveḷi naṭuvē varaiyō tarucuka vāḻkkaimeyp poruḷē
translation: O True Substance, a life of boundless bliss in the center of the expanse of Siva, within the thirteenth state.
commentary: The experience deepens from a central point to a vast space. In the thirteenth state, one enters the "expanse of Siva," a boundless realm of pure consciousness where life is simply unending, limitless bliss.

translit: īreṇ ṇilaiyeṉa viyampumē ṉilaiyiṟ pūraṇa cukamāyp poruntumeyp poruḷē
translation: O True Substance, who abides as perfect bliss in the supreme state known as the sixteenth state.
commentary: The ascent through the inner planes reaches a culmination. In what is called the sixteenth and supreme state, the divine is experienced as total and perfect bliss.

translit: ellā nilaikaḷu micaintāṅ kāṅkē ellā māki yilaṅkumeyp poruḷē
translation: O True Substance, who harmoniously resides in all states and, becoming everything, shines in each and every place.
commentary: After leading us up a ladder of progressively higher spiritual states, this verse reveals a deeper truth. The divine is more than at the peak; it exists harmoniously within all levels and, in fact, becomes everything, shining everywhere.

translit: maṉātikaḷ poruntā vāṉaṭu vāṉāy aṉātiyuṇ maiyatā yamarntameyp poruḷē
translation: O True Substance, established as beginningless Reality, the space within space, inaccessible to the mind and its faculties.
commentary: The ultimate nature of the divine is beyond all the states just described. It is the reality that has no beginning, the foundational space within which even space itself exists. Because it is so fundamental, it cannot be grasped by the mind or the senses.

translit: tāṉoru tāṉāyt tāṉē tāṉāy ūṉuyir viḷakku morutaṉip poruḷē
translation: O singular, unique substance, existing as the One alone, being yourself by yourself, you illuminate body and life.
commentary: The divine is utterly self-existent, depending on nothing else for its being. It is this singular reality that animates all creatures, providing the light of consciousness to both body and life.

translit: atuviṉu ḷatuvā yatuvē yatuvāyp potuviṉuḷ naṭikkum pūraṇap poruḷē
translation: O perfect substance, being That within that, being That itself, you dance within the universal expanse.
commentary: The supreme reality is often called "That" (atu) to signify it is beyond all names and descriptions. This reality is both the essence within all things and the totality of all things, a paradox showing its all-encompassing nature. This divine play unfolds in the universal space of consciousness, accessible to all.

translit: iyalpiṉu ḷiyalpā yiyalpē yiyalpā uyaluṟa viḷaṅku morutaṉip poruḷē
translation: O singular, unique substance, being the nature within nature, being nature itself, you manifest to grant salvation.
commentary: The divine is the fundamental nature (iyalpu) of existence itself. It is more than found in nature; it is nature. The purpose of this manifestation is to help beings achieve liberation.

translit: aruviṉu ḷaruvā yaruvaru varuvāy uruviṉuḷ viḷaṅku moruparam poruḷē
translation: O singular, supreme substance, you are formless within the formless, you are the formless within form, and you shine forth from within form.
commentary: God exists in a state of pure formlessness (aruvu) but also dwells as the formless essence inside every visible form (uruvu). From within these very forms, its presence can be perceived.

translit: alakilāc cittā yatunilai yatuvāy ulakelām viḷaṅku morutaṉip poruḷē
translation: O singular, unique substance, being immeasurable consciousness, being that state itself, you illuminate all the worlds.
commentary: The divine substance is described here as limitless consciousness (citt). It is more than an entity that possesses consciousness; it is the state of consciousness itself. This infinite awareness is the light that makes all worlds and all experiences possible.

translit: poruḷiṉuṭ poruḷāyp poruḷatu poruḷā yorumaiyiṉ viḷaṅku morutaṉip poruḷē
translation: O singular, unique Substance, shining in oneness, you are the substance within substance and the substance of that very substance.
commentary: God is the ultimate reality, the essence that makes everything else real. This verse explains that God is the "substance within substance," meaning the core reality inside every object, person, and idea. All things are united in this one fundamental existence.

translit: āṭuṟu cittika ḷaṟupattu nāṉkeḻu kōṭiyum viḷaṅkak kulavumeyp poruḷē
translation: O true Substance, gloriously manifesting the sixty-four performing siddhis and seventy million more.
commentary: All extraordinary or supernatural powers (siddhis) originate from God. While traditions list a set number of these powers, like the sixty-four mentioned here, Vallalar uses vast numbers to show that the divine potential is infinite.

translit: kūṭṭuṟu cittikaḷ kōṭipal kōṭiyum āṭṭuṟa viḷaṅku marumperum poruḷē
translation: O rare and great Substance, who animates and manifests crores upon many crores of composite siddhis.
commentary: Even the most complex powers are animated by the one divine Substance. The verse mentions "composite siddhis," which are powers formed by combining others. No matter how complex these abilities become, they are not independent but are directed and made active by God alone.

translit: aṟivuṟu cittika ḷaṉantakō ṭikaḷum piṟivaṟa viḷakkum peruntaṉip poruḷē
translation: O great, unique Substance, who indivisibly illuminates endless crores of siddhis of knowledge.
commentary: God is the single, undivided source of all powers related to knowledge and consciousness. These "siddhis of knowledge" are forms of enlightened awareness, and they are not separate from God. They are direct, inseparable expressions of the one divine mind.

translit: vīṭuka ḷellām vitineṟi viḷaṅka āṭalcey taruḷu marumperum poruḷē
translation: O rare and great Substance, who graciously performs the dance that illuminates the ordained paths to all states of liberation.
commentary: God's cosmic activity reveals the ways to spiritual freedom. Liberation (vīṭu) means release from the cycle of birth and death. The divine "dance" (āṭal) is a classic image for God's action in the world, and this dance illuminates the many valid paths a soul can follow to attain that final state of freedom.

translit: paṟṟuka ḷellām patineṟi viḷaṅka uṟṟaru ḷāṭalcey yorutaṉip poruḷē
translation: O singular, unique Substance, who performs the sacred play of grace, having come to make the path of the Lord shine clear by removing all attachments.
commentary: Our attachments to the world are what prevent us from seeing clearly. God's grace actively works to remove these attachments, and once they are gone, the path to the Lord (pati neṟi) becomes obvious and easy to follow.

translit: parattiṉiṟ paramē parattiṉmēṟ paramē parattiṉuṭ paramē paramparam paramē
translation: O Supreme within the Supreme! O Supreme above the Supreme! O Supreme inside the Supreme! O Supreme, the ultimate Supreme!
commentary: Repetition expresses the all-encompassing nature of God. By calling the Divine the Supreme within, above, and inside the Supreme, Vallalar shows that God is the absolute reality in every possible dimension, both beyond the world and at its very heart.

translit: parampeṟum paramē parantarum paramē parampatam paramē parañ citamparamē
translation: O Supreme, the highest attainment! O Supreme, who grants the highest state! O Supreme, the highest abode! O Supreme, the highest Chidambaram!
commentary: God is both the goal of the spiritual path and the one who makes reaching that goal possible. The Divine is the highest state to be attained (parampadam), the giver of that state, and the pure space of consciousness (parañ citamparam) in which it is realized.

translit: parampukaḻ paramē parampakar paramē parañcuka paramē parañciva paramē
translation: O Supreme, praised by the highest ones! O Supreme, proclaimed by the highest ones! O Supreme, who is supreme bliss! O Supreme, who is supreme Sivam!
commentary: The highest reality is recognized by those who have reached the highest spiritual states. This reality is experienced as supreme bliss (parañjukam) and is identified with Sivam, the ultimate source of all that is good and auspicious in the universe.

translit: paraṅkoḷciṟ paramē parañceytaṟ paramē taraṅkoḷpoṟ paramē taṉipperum paramē
translation: O supreme space of consciousness that holds the Supreme! O Supreme Self that performs the supreme act! O golden supreme space of perfect quality! O singular, great Supreme
commentary: God is described here as the ultimate consciousness that contains all things (paraṅkoḷciṟ param) and the ultimate agent behind all action (parañceytaṟ param). The reference to a "golden" supreme space suggests its perfection, purity, and immeasurable value.

translit: varamparā paramē vaṇamparā paramē paramparā paramē patamparā paramē
translation: O Supreme beyond limits! O Supreme beyond worship! O Supreme beyond the beyond! O Supreme beyond the final state!
commentary: God is described as a reality so vast it transcends all our categories for understanding it. It is beyond physical or mental limits and even beyond our acts of worship. It is "beyond the beyond," a powerful image for something that exceeds our ultimate concepts, including the very idea of a final spiritual state (padam).

translit: cattiya patamē cattuva patamē nittiya patamē niṟkuṇa patamē
translation: O State of Truth! O State of pure being! O eternal State! O attributeless State!
commentary: God is presented here as a person and as the ultimate state of existence (padam). This state is defined by absolute truth (satya), pure being (sattva), and eternity (nitya). Crucially, it is also nirguna, a state without any limiting qualities or attributes, a pure and unconditioned reality.

translit: tattuva patamē taṟpata patamē cittuṟu patamē ciṟcuka patamē
translation: O State of reality! O State of the Absolute! O State imbued with consciousness! O State of the bliss of consciousness!
commentary: The ultimate state (padam) is further described as the very principle of reality (tattva) and the Absolute itself (tat-pada). This is not a void or an empty state; it is filled with pure consciousness (cit) and is the source of conscious bliss (cit-sukha).

translit: tamparam patamē taṉiccukam patamē amparam patamē yaruṭparam patamē
translation: O State of the Supreme Self! O State of unique bliss! O State of the cosmic expanse! O State of supreme Grace!
commentary: This divine state is identical with the Supreme Self (tat-param), a condition of unique and singular bliss. It is also the vast cosmic expanse (ambaram) and, most importantly for the seeker, the state of supreme Grace (arul).

translit: tantira patamē cantira patamē mantira patamē mantaṇa patamē
translation: O State of Tantra! O State of the Moon! O State of Mantra! O State of the great secret
commentary: The ultimate state is the source and goal of all spiritual paths. It is the reality behind Tantra (spiritual disciplines) and Mantra (sacred sounds). It embodies the cool, peaceful light of the moon and is the great secret (manthanam) that all spiritual traditions seek to uncover.

translit: navantaru patamē naṭantaru patamē civantaru patamē civaciva patamē
translation: The foot that bestows the nine states, the foot that bestows the dance, the foot that bestows Sivam, the foot that is Siva, Siva.
commentary: The "foot" is a traditional symbol for God's grace, the point of contact between the divine and the world. This grace is not static; it is the creative power that manifests as the cosmic dance, bestows higher states of consciousness, and ultimately reveals the nature of reality itself, which is Sivam (the ultimate auspiciousness).

translit: piramameyk katiyē piramameyp patiyē piramaniṟ kuṇamē piramaciṟ kuṇamē
translation: The true goal that is Brahmam, the true Lord that is Brahmam. Brahmam as the attributeless nature, Brahmam as the nature of pure consciousness.
commentary: The ultimate reality, Brahmam, is both the path and the destination. Vallalar presents two aspects of it: nirgunam, where it is the absolute beyond all qualities and descriptions, and citgunam, where its essential nature is knowable as pure consciousness.

translit: piramamē piramap perunilai micaiyuṟum paramamē parama patantaruñ civamē
translation: Brahmam itself, the Supreme Reality abiding above the great state of Brahmam, the Sivam that bestows the supreme state.
commentary: Just as the idea of Brahmam (the Absolute Reality) is presented, Vallalar points to a reality that is even beyond it. He calls this Sivam, the supreme truth that grants the ultimate state. This suggests a spiritual path that continually opens into ever-deeper realizations, beyond even the highest philosophical concepts.

translit: avaṉō ṭavaḷā yatuvā yalavāy navamā nilaimicai naṇṇiya civamē
translation: Being He, She, It, and That which is not, it is the Sivam that abides upon the wondrous new state.
commentary: The ultimate reality, Sivam, transcends all human categories. It is masculine, feminine, neuter, and even the nothingness that lies beyond all forms of being. This all-encompassing truth, Vallalar says, is realized in a "wondrous new state," a direct experience that goes beyond old definitions.

translit: emporu ḷāki yemakkaruḷ puriyuñ cemporu ḷākiya civamē civamē
translation: Becoming our very substance and bestowing grace upon us, it is the Perfect Reality, Sivam, Sivam
commentary: This is the ultimate intimacy with God. The Perfect Reality (Sem-porul) is not a distant being but becomes our very own substance, our deepest self. It is from this place of complete union that grace flows, prompting the ecstatic repetition of "Sivam, Sivam."

translit: orunilai yituvē vuyarnilai yeṉumoru tirunilai mēviya civamē civamē
translation: O Sivam, Sivam, who has reached the one sacred state declared as the supreme state, this very state.
commentary: There is only one supreme state of being, and it is the state of Sivam itself. This is the ultimate goal, a sacred condition where the divine essence is fully realized.

translit: meyvait taḻiyā veṟuveḷi naṭuvuṟu teyvap patiyāñ civamē civamē
translation: O Sivam, Sivam, the divine Lord who, having established truth, dwells in the center of the indestructible vast space.
commentary: The divine is found as the absolute truth at the center of the vast, formless space of pure consciousness. This space (veṟuveḷi) is not empty but is the indestructible ground of all reality, with Sivam as its heart.

translit: puraitavirt teṉakkē poṉmuṭi cūṭṭic ciramuṟa nāṭṭiya civamē civamē
translation: O Sivam, Sivam, who removed my faults, crowned me alone with a golden crown, and fixed it firmly upon my head.
commentary: Grace is profoundly intimate. The divine removes all personal flaws and bestows the ultimate spiritual honor, symbolized by a golden crown, marking the soul's irreversible transformation.

translit: kalviyuñ cākāk kalviyu maḻiyāc celvamu maḷitta civamē civamē
translation: O Sivam, Sivam, who gave me knowledge, and the deathless knowledge, and imperishable wealth.
commentary: The divine bestows two kinds of gifts. It gives worldly knowledge, but more importantly, it grants the "deathless knowledge" which is the direct experience of immortality, and the "imperishable wealth" of unending grace.

translit: aruḷamu teṉakkē yaḷittaru ṇeṟivāyt teruḷuṟa vaḷarkkuñ civamē civamē
translation: O Sivam, Sivam, who gives me alone the ambrosia of grace and nurtures me on the path of grace so that I attain clarity.
commentary: Grace is a concept and a substance, an "ambrosia" that nourishes the soul. The divine feeds the seeker this grace, guiding them along the spiritual path until they achieve perfect, unclouded clarity.

translit: cattelā mākiyun tāṉoru tāṉāñ cittelām vallatōr tiruvaruṭ civamē
translation: The Sivam of sacred grace, which is all existence yet also singularly itself, capable of all things through its consciousness.
commentary: God, called Sivam, has a dual nature. It is all of existence (sat), the substance of everything in the universe, yet it is also a unique, singular being that transcends creation. Its infinite power comes from pure consciousness (cit).

translit: eṅkē karuṇai yiyaṟkaiyi ṉuḷḷaṉa aṅkē viḷaṅkiya varuṭperuñ civamē
translation: The great, gracious Sivam, which shines forth wherever natural compassion exists.
commentary: The divine presence is not confined to sacred places or rituals. God, or Sivam, is said to manifest wherever there is natural, unforced compassion. This makes an ethical feeling the very location where the divine appears in the world.

translit: yārē yeṉṉiṉu miraṅkukiṉ ṟārkkuc cīrē yaḷikkuñ citampara civamē
translation: The Sivam of Chidambaram, which grants greatness to those who are compassionate, regardless of who they are.
commentary: Divine reward is not based on one's religion, social standing, or background; "greatness" is granted to anyone who shows compassion. God, called Sivam of Chidambaram (the inner space of consciousness), responds to this one quality above all others.

translit: poynneṟi yaṉaittiṉum pukuttā teṉaiyaruṭ cenneṟi celuttiya ciṟcapaic civamē
translation: The Sivam of the Chit Sabhai, which guided me onto the true path of grace, preventing me from entering any false paths.
commentary: Spiritual progress is not simply a matter of human effort. The divine, experienced in the Chit Sabhai (the inner hall of consciousness), actively guides the soul. It acts as a protective force, steering one away from false doctrines and onto the one true path of grace.

translit: kollā neṟiyē kuruvaru ṇeṟiyeṉap palkā leṉakkup pakarntameyc civamē
translation: The true Sivam, which declared to me again and again that the path of non-killing is the path of the Guru's grace.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual law, received directly from God (Sivam), is this: the path of grace is the path of non-killing. Vallalar states that this truth was not learned from scriptures but was declared to him repeatedly by the divine itself, making absolute non-violence the foundation of his teaching.

translit: uyirelām potuvi ṉuḷampaṭa nōkkuka ceyirelām viṭukeṉac ceppiya civamē
translation: The Sivam who declared: 'See all lives impartially, embracing them with your heart; abandon all faults.'
commentary: True spiritual practice means seeing every living being as equal, without prejudice or preference. Embracing all life with this impartial love is the direct method for letting go of one's own faults and impurities.

translit: payirppuṟu karaṇap paricukaḷ paṟpala uyirttira ḷoṉṟeṉa vuraittameyc civamē
translation: The true Sivam who declared that the multitude of lives is one, despite the many and various repulsive sensations produced by the inner faculties.
commentary: Our minds and senses often create feelings of separation, disgust, or repulsion toward others. God's teaching reveals this is an illusion. The ultimate truth is that all life is a single, unified whole, and we must learn to see past our own internal reactions to perceive this unity.

translit: uyiruḷyā memmu ḷuyirivai yuṇarntē uyirnalam paravukeṉ ṟuraittameyc civamē
translation: The true Sivam who declared: 'I am within life, and life is within Me. Realizing this, promote the well-being of life.'
commentary: God is not a distant being but a presence dwelling within every living thing, just as every living thing exists within God. Because of this intimate connection, the highest spiritual action is to care for life. Promoting the well-being of others is the most direct way to honor the divine.

translit: iyalaru ḷoḷiyō rēkatē cattiṉām uyiroḷi kāṇkaveṉ ṟuraittameyc civamē
translation: The true Sivam who declared: 'See the light of the soul as a fraction of the inherent light of Grace.'
commentary: The light or consciousness of an individual soul is not separate from God. It is a small spark, a single ray, of the infinite light of divine Grace (arul). Realizing this helps dissolve the ego's sense of being a separate self and reveals our true nature as part of the divine whole.

translit: aruḷalā taṇuvu macaintiṭā tataṉāl aruṇalam paravukeṉ ṟaṟaintameyc civamē
translation: The true Sivam who proclaimed: 'Not even an atom moves without Grace; therefore, promote the excellence of Grace.'
commentary: Divine Grace (arul) is the fundamental force that animates the entire universe, from the smallest particle to the largest star. Since everything is powered by this grace, the purpose of human life is to align with it. To "promote the excellence of Grace" means to live a life of compassion, making that divine quality more active and visible in the world.

translit: aruḷuṟi ṉellā mākumī tuṇmai aruḷuṟa muyalkaveṉ ṟaruḷiya civamē
translation: O Sivam, who graciously taught me: “If you attain Grace, all things become possible. This is the truth. Strive to attain Grace.”
commentary: Grace is the key that unlocks all possibilities and makes anything achievable. This is presented as a direct, simple truth from God (Sivam, the ultimate reality). The verse is a call to action: since Grace is the source of all capability, the most vital spiritual work is to actively strive to attain it.

translit: aruṇeṟi yoṉṟē teruṇeṟi maṟṟelām iruṇeṟi yeṉaveṉak kiyampiya civamē
translation: O Sivam, who proclaimed to me: “The path of Grace alone is the path of clarity. All other paths are paths of darkness.”
commentary: The only path to true spiritual clarity is the one centered on attaining Grace. All other approaches, including religious rituals or intellectual studies that lack this focus, are considered paths of darkness and confusion. This verse simplifies the spiritual quest, identifying the direct experience of Grace as the sole objective.

translit: aruḷpeṟiṟ ṟurumpumō raintoḻil puriyun teruḷitu veṉavē ceppiya civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: “If Grace is obtained, even a speck of dust can perform the five cosmic functions. This is the clear truth.”
commentary: The power of Grace is absolute. To illustrate this, Vallalar uses a startling image: if imbued with Grace, even a lifeless speck of dust could perform the five cosmic functions of creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and revelation, which belong to God alone. Grace is more than a blessing; it is the direct infusion of divine power that can transform anything into an agent of the divine.

translit: aruḷaṟi voṉṟē yaṟivumaṟ ṟellām maruḷaṟi veṉṟē vakuttameyc civamē
translation: O true Sivam, who laid down the principle: “Knowledge of Grace alone is true knowledge; all other knowledge is the knowledge of delusion.”
commentary: True knowledge is not intellectual learning or scriptural mastery, but the direct, felt experience of Grace. All other forms of knowledge, no matter how profound they seem, are ultimately a kind of delusion (maruḷ). This shifts the goal of wisdom from accumulating information in the mind to achieving a state of being in the heart.

translit: aruṭcuka moṉṟē yarumpeṟaṟ peruñcukam maruṭcukam piṟaveṉa vakuttameyc civamē
translation: O true Sivam, who laid down the principle: “The bliss of Grace alone is the great, rarely attained bliss. All other forms of bliss are the bliss of delusion.”
commentary: The only genuine and lasting happiness is the bliss experienced through Grace. All other forms of pleasure, from the sensory to the intellectual, are temporary and ultimately deceptive, a kind of bliss born of delusion (maruḷ). This directs the search for fulfillment away from the external world and toward the inner state that Grace makes possible.

translit: aruṭpē ṟatuvē yarumpeṟaṟ perumpē ṟiruṭpē ṟaṟukkumeṉ ṟiyampiya civamē
translation: The gift of grace is the great gift, difficult to obtain; it will sever the state of darkness, declared the benevolent Sivam.
commentary: Grace is the ultimate gift because it has the power to destroy the 'state of darkness' (iruṭpēṟu). This darkness is the soul's fundamental ignorance and separation from the divine, and only grace can permanently remove it.

translit: aruṭṭaṉi vallapa matuvē yelāñcey poruṭṭaṉic citteṉap pukaṉṟameyc civamē
translation: The unique power of grace is the singular substance, the consciousness-force that accomplishes everything, proclaimed the true Sivam.
commentary: Grace is more than a passive blessing from God; it is the very consciousness-force that makes everything happen. Vallalar identifies it as the 'singular substance' (poruṭṭaṉic cit), the dynamic power that creates and sustains the universe.

translit: aruḷaṟi yārtamai yaṟiyār emmaiyum poruḷaṟi yāreṉap pukaṉṟameyc civamē
translation: Those who do not know grace do not know themselves, and they do not know the substance of Us either, proclaimed the true Sivam.
commentary: To know grace is to know yourself and to know God. Without an experience of grace, true self-knowledge and an understanding of the divine reality are impossible.

translit: aruṇilai yoṉṟē yaṉaittum peṟunilai poruṇilai kāṇkeṉap pukaṉṟameyc civamē
translation: The state of grace alone is the state in which one obtains everything; realize this state of substance, proclaimed the true Sivam.
commentary: The state of grace is the state of ultimate fulfillment where one gains everything of true and lasting value. The verse urges us to realize this 'state of substance' (poruṇilai), as it is the supreme goal containing all others.

translit: aruḷvaṭi vatuvē yaḻiyāt taṉivaṭi varuḷpeṟa muyalukeṉ ṟaruḷiya civamē
translation: The form of grace is the immortal, unique form; strive to obtain grace, graced the benevolent Sivam.
commentary: The essential nature of reality is the form of grace (aruḷ vaṭivam), and it is immortal. The purpose of life, therefore, is simple: strive with all your being to attain this grace.

translit: aruḷē nammiya laruḷē nammuru aruḷē namvaṭi vāmeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our nature, Grace is Our form, Grace is Our very body."
commentary: Here God reveals God's own nature. Grace is not only something God gives: it is the very essence, form and body of the Divine.

translit: aruḷē nammaṭi yaruḷē nammuṭi aruḷē namnaṭu vāmeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our feet, Grace is Our head, Grace is Our center."
commentary: Sivam declares that the whole divine form is Grace: from the feet (aṭi) to the crown (muṭi), and at the centre (naṭu). The ultimate reality is made of nothing but grace.

translit: aruḷē nammaṟi varuḷē nammaṉam aruḷē naṅkuṇa māmeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our intelligence, Grace is Our mind, Grace is Our character."
commentary: Sivam declares that the divine intelligence, mind and character are all Grace. God's consciousness and qualities are pure grace.

translit: aruḷē nampati yaruḷē nampatam aruḷē nammiṭa māmeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our abode, Grace is Our state, Grace is Our very place."
commentary: Sivam's abode (pati), state (patam) and place (iṭam) are Grace. The Divine dwells in no physical place, only in grace.

translit: aruḷē nantuṇai yaruḷē nantoḻil aruḷē namvirup pāmeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our companion, Grace is Our action, Grace is Our desire."
commentary: Sivam's companion, work and will are all Grace. God's every act and intention is moved by grace.

translit: aruḷē namporu ḷaruḷē nammoḷi aruḷē nāmaṟi vāyeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our substance, Grace is Our light, Grace is what We are: know this."
commentary: Sivam's substance, light and very Self are Grace, and the soul is told to know it.

translit: aruḷē naṅkula maruḷē nammiṉam aruḷē nāmaṟi vāyeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our lineage, Grace is Our kin, Grace is what We are: know this."
commentary: Even lineage and kin, the markers by which people divide themselves, are for God nothing but Grace. God is wholly identified with this supreme compassion.

translit: aruḷē nañcuka maruḷē nampeyar aruḷē nāmaṟi vāyeṉṟa civamē
translation: O Sivam, who declared: "Grace is Our bliss, Grace is Our name, Grace is what We are: know this."
commentary: God's bliss and even God's name are Grace. Grace is not an attribute of God; it is God's whole identity.

translit: aruḷoḷi yaṭaintaṉai yaruḷamu tuṇṭaṉai aruṇmati vāḻkaveṉ ṟaruḷiya civamē
translation: O Sivam, who graciously blessed me, saying: "You have attained the Light of Grace, you have drunk the nectar of Grace. May your wisdom of Grace flourish!"
