commentary: God does not only give grace; God blesses Vallalar to flourish without end. This treasure gives the highest prize: a life that does not die, thriving through the ages.

translit: itamuṟa vūḻitō ṟeṭutteṭut tulakōrk kutaviṉu mulavā tōṅkunaṉ ṉitiyē
translation: O good treasure that flourishes without being depleted, even when benevolently drawn from again and again through the eons to help the people of the world.
commentary: This divine treasure is meant to be shared. It is an infinite source of help for all humanity, and giving it away freely does not diminish it in the slightest.

translit: iruniti yeḻuniti yiyaṉava nitimutaṟ ṟiruniti yellān tarumoru nitiyē
translation: O the one treasure that bestows the two treasures, the seven treasures, the nine noble treasures, and all other sacred treasures.
commentary: All other forms of wealth, both spiritual and material, come from this one supreme treasure. The "two, seven, and nine treasures" are traditional ways of listing all possible kinds of prosperity, and Vallalar states that divine grace is the source of them all.

translit: evvakai nitikaḷu mintamā nitiyiṭai avvakai kiṭaikkumeṉ ṟaruḷiya nitiyē
translation: O treasure that graciously declared, "Every kind of treasure can be found within this great treasure."
commentary: God himself confirms that this one "great treasure" of grace is complete. Nothing else is needed, because every other gift or form of wealth is already contained within it.

translit: aṟputam viḷaṅku maruṭperu nitiyē kaṟpaṉai kaṭanta karuṇaimā nitiyē
translation: O great treasure of grace where miracles manifest, O great treasure of compassion that transcends all conception.
commentary: This ultimate treasure is the very source from which miracles arise. At its core, it is a form of compassion so profound and vast that the human mind cannot fully grasp it.

translit: naṟkuṇa nitiyē caṟkuṇa nitiyē niṟkuṇa nitiyē ciṟkuṇa nitiyē
translation: O treasury of good qualities, O treasury of the qualities of pure Being, O treasury of the quality-less, O treasury of the qualities of pure Consciousness.
commentary: Seemingly opposite terms capture the nature of God. God is sarkuṇam (possessing all good qualities), yet also nirkuṇam (the formless Absolute beyond any quality). God is the source of pure consciousness (sirkuṇam) and the embodiment of all goodness (naṟkuṇam). This shows a God who is both personal and relatable, and simultaneously the ultimate, impersonal reality.

translit: paḷakilā tōṅkum paḷikkumā malaiyē vaḷamelā niṟainta māṇikka malaiyē
translation: O great mountain of flawless, towering crystal, O mountain of rubies filled with all abundance.
commentary: God is compared to two great mountains, each representing a divine aspect. The mountain of flawless crystal symbolizes absolute purity and clarity. The mountain of rubies represents unimaginable value, richness, and abundance.

translit: matiyuṟa viḷaṅku marakata malaiyē vatitaru pēroḷi vaccira malaiyē
translation: O mountain of emerald, gleaming with the coolness of the moon, O mountain of diamond, where a great light dwells.
commentary: The mountain imagery continues, with emerald suggesting a soothing, cool grace like moonlight. The diamond mountain represents God's indestructible nature and the brilliant, inner light that shines from within ultimate reality.

translit: uraimaṉaṅ kaṭantāṅ kōṅkupoṉ malaiyē turiyamēl veḷiyiṟ jōtimā malaiyē
translation: O golden mountain, towering beyond speech and mind, O great mountain of Jothi in the space beyond Turiya
commentary: The metaphors now move beyond the physical world to the purely spiritual. God is a golden mountain beyond the reach of human thought or words. He is also a mountain of pure Light (Jothi) that exists in a sublime space beyond Turiya, the fourth state of consciousness that transcends waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.

translit: puṟputan tirainurai puraimuta lilatōr aṟputak kaṭalē yamutattaṇ kaṭalē
translation: O wondrous sea, without bubble, wave, foam, or any such flaw! O cool sea of nectar
commentary: Here the central image shifts from a solid mountain to a boundless sea. God is an ocean without waves, foam, or bubbles, a symbol of perfect, eternal calm, free from all disturbance. This is not an empty stillness but a blissful, cool sea of nectar, offering sweetness and immortality.

translit: iruṭkalai tavirttoḷi yellām vaḻaṅkiya aruṭperuṅ kaṭalē yāṉantak kaṭalē
translation: O vast ocean of grace, O ocean of bliss, who dispelled the arts of darkness and bestowed all light!
commentary: God is the source of all light and bliss. The experience of the divine is the presence of something good and the active removal of all that is dark, ignorant, and painful.

translit: pavakkaṭal kaṭantunāṉ pārttapō tarukē uvappuṟu vaḷaṅkoṇ ṭōṅkiya karaiyē
translation: O lofty shore, rich with joyous abundance, that I saw nearby after crossing the ocean of birth.
commentary: The cycle of repeated birth and death is often imagined as a vast, turbulent ocean. God is the safe and beautiful shore you finally reach after that long journey, a place of joyful peace that appears right beside you the moment the crossing is complete.

translit: eṉṟuyarc cōṭaika ḷellān tavirttuḷa naṉṟuṟa viḷaṅkiya nantaṉak kāvē
translation: O pleasure grove, shining splendidly in my heart, after removing all the weariness of my suffering.
commentary: The divine presence is not a distant reality but a beautiful pleasure garden that can bloom within your own heart. Its appearance brings an end to all the suffering and weariness of life.

translit: cēṟṟunī riṉṟinaṟ ṟīñcuvai tarumōr ūṟṟunīr nirampa vuṭaiyapūn taṭamē
translation: O flower-filled pond, brimming with the water of a sweet-tasting spring, completely without mud.
commentary: The experience of God is like drinking from a pure, sweet spring. It is endlessly refreshing because it is completely free of the "mud" of worldly confusion, desire, and impurity.

translit: kōṭaivāy virinta kuḷirtaru niḻalē mēṭaivāy vīciya melliya kāṟṟē
translation: O cool shade spreading wide in the heat of summer! O gentle breeze blowing across a raised platform
commentary: The feeling of God's presence is one of profound comfort and relief. It is as soothing to the soul as cool shade on a hot day or a gentle breeze after a long climb.

translit: kaḷaippaṟak kiṭaitta karuṇainaṉ ṉīrē iḷaippaṟa vāytta viṉcuvai yuṇavē
translation: O good water of compassion, received to remove weariness! O sweet-tasting food, provided to remove exhaustion!
commentary: Grace is a concept and the true sustenance that ends our deepest spiritual exhaustion. It is explicitly called the "water of compassion," the only thing that can quench the soul's thirst and fatigue.

translit: teṉṉaivāyk kiṭaitta cevviḷa nīrē teṉṉaivāṉ palattiṟ ṟirukutīm pālē
translation: O choice tender coconut water from the palm! O rich, sweet milk from the palm's great fruit!
commentary: These images describe grace as something natural, pure, and delightful. Like tender coconut water, it is a pristine and refreshing gift, perfectly sealed and offered for our enjoyment.

translit: nīrnacai tavirkku nelliyaṅ kaṉiyē vērviḷai palaviṉ meṉcuvaic cuḷaiyē
translation: O fine gooseberry fruit that quenches thirst! O soft, sweet segment from the jackfruit that fruits at its root!
commentary: The experience of grace can transform our perception, just as the Indian gooseberry makes plain water taste sweet. It can also arise from humble and unexpected places, like the jackfruit that grows at the tree's very root, reminding us that divine help is always near.

translit: kaṭṭumām paḻamē katalivāṉ paḻamē iṭṭanaṟ cuvaicey yilantaiyaṅ kaṉiyē
translation: O grafted mango fruit! O great banana fruit! O beautiful jujube fruit, yielding a welcome, good taste!
commentary: The variety of fruits suggests that the experience of the divine is not monolithic. It offers a spectrum of spiritual tastes, from the common and beloved banana to the cultivated perfection of a grafted mango, each providing its own unique joy.

translit: puṉitavāṉ ṟaruviṟ putumaiyām palamē kaṉiyelāṅ kūṭṭik kalantatīñ cuvaiyē
translation: O wondrous new fruit from the sacred celestial tree! O sweet taste made by blending all fruits together
commentary: These final images describe the ultimate divine experience in two ways. It is a completely new taste from a celestial realm, unlike anything on earth, and it is also the essence of all earthly joys combined into one perfect flavor.

translit: itantaru karumpi leṭuttatīñ cāṟē patantaru vellap pākiṉiṉ cuvaiyē
translation: You are the sweet juice pressed from life-giving sugarcane, the taste of perfectly prepared jaggery syrup.
commentary: Here, the sweetness of God is found in raw nature and in something carefully prepared. Like sugarcane juice or jaggery (unrefined sugar syrup), the divine taste is concentrated through a process, suggesting that spiritual refinement brings out a deeper, more potent experience.

translit: cālavē yiṉikkuñ carkkarait tiraḷē ēlavē nāvuk kiṉiyakaṟ kaṇṭē
translation: You are a mass of exceedingly sweet sugar, the rock candy perfectly pleasant to the tongue.
commentary: The experience of the divine is not a faint or distant thing; it is an intense, overwhelming, and deeply satisfying sweetness. Likening it to a lump of sugar or rock candy emphasizes its pure, concentrated power to delight the senses of the soul.

translit: ulappuṟā tiṉikku muyarmalait tēṉē kalappuṟā maturaṅ kaṉintakōṟ ṟēṉē
translation: You are the honey from high mountains, sweetening without end, the comb honey ripened into pure sweetness.
commentary: This divine sweetness is natural, pure, and unending, like wild honey gathered from a high, untouched place. It is a taste that never spoils or runs out, a constant and reliable source of joy.

translit: navaiyilā teṉakku naṇṇiya naṟavē cuvaiyelān tiraṭṭiya tūyatīm patamē
translation: You are the flawless nectar that has reached me, the pure, sweet delicacy embodying all flavors.
commentary: All the different tastes of the world are gathered into one flawless, ultimate sweetness. This is the divine nectar, the essence of all pleasure, which Vallalar celebrates as having finally reached him personally.

translit: patampeṟak kāycciya pacunaṟum pālē itampeṟa vurukkiya viḷampacu neyyē
translation: You are fragrant cow's milk boiled to perfection, fresh cow's ghee rendered to be wholesome.
commentary: The divine presence is a momentary pleasure and a source of deep, life-giving nourishment, like warm milk or wholesome ghee (clarified butter). The careful act of boiling the milk or rendering the ghee suggests that this divine sustenance is most potent when prepared with care and attention.

translit: ularntiṭā teṉṟu morupaṭit tāki malarntunal vaṇṇam vayaṅkiya malarē
translation: O Flower that never withers, that is ever unchanging, that has blossomed and shines with beautiful color.
commentary: A normal flower blossoms and then fades. The divine is a flower that is eternally in full bloom, a symbol of beauty and life that never withers or decays. It represents a state of permanent, radiant perfection.

translit: ikantaru puvimuta levvula kuyirkaḷum ukantiṭa maṇakkuñ cukantanaṉ maṇamē
translation: O sweet, good fragrance that all beings, from this world onward to every other world, delight in and savor.
commentary: The experience of the divine is not limited to one person or one place. It is described as a universal fragrance that permeates all worlds, bringing joy to every living being that encounters it.

translit: yāḻuṟu micaiyē yiṉiyaviṉ ṉicaiyē ēḻuṟu micaiyē yiyalaru ḷicaiyē
translation: O melody from the yaazh! O sweet, pleasing melody! O melody of the seven notes! O melody that is the very nature of grace!
commentary: God is described as the perfect melody, a music that encompasses all possible notes. This divine music is more than beautiful, it is the audible form of grace itself.

translit: tivaḷoḷip paruvañ cērntanal lavaḷē avaḷoṭuṅ kūṭi yaṭaintatōr cukamē
translation: O the singular bliss attained by uniting with Her, the good one who has reached the age of radiant light!
commentary: Here, the divine is addressed as a feminine power, a radiant being whose union brings a state of unparalleled bliss. This points to the mystical experience of merging the individual self with the divine partner, a state of perfect joy and completion.

translit: nātanal varaippi ṉaṇṇiya pāṭṭē vētakī tattil viḷaitirup pāṭṭē
translation: O song found within the good domain of Natham! O sacred song that arises from the music of the Vedas
commentary: The divine is both the source of sound itself, the primordial vibration called Natham (primordial sound), and the sacred truth expressed in the music of the Vedas (ancient sacred texts). This connects the unmanifest, universal sound with its expression in holy scripture.

translit: naṉmārkkar nāvi ṉaviṟṟiya pāṭṭē caṉmārkka caṅkan taḻuviya pāṭṭē
translation: The very song uttered by the tongues of those on the good path, the very song embraced by the Sanmarkkam assembly.
commentary: This divine song is more than an abstract concept; it is the very truth spoken by those who follow the right path. Vallalar says it is the song embraced by his own Sanmarkkam (True Path) community, making this universal truth the core of his specific teachings.

translit: nampuṟu mākama naviṟṟiya pāṭṭē empala mākiya vampalap pāṭṭē
translation: The very song proclaimed by the revered Agamas, the very song of the Ambalam that is our strength.
commentary: The divine song is also the essence of the revered scriptures known as the Agamas and the vibration of the Ambalam (the sacred space of consciousness). For Vallalar, this sacred space is both the cosmos and a reality to be experienced within oneself.

translit: eṉmaṉak kaṇṇē eṉṉaruṭ kaṇṇē eṉṉiru kaṇṇē yeṉkaṇuṇ maṇiyē
translation: My mind's eye, my eye of grace, my two eyes, the very pupil within my eye.
commentary: The focus shifts from the divine as an external song to an intimate, internal reality. God is seen and is the very instrument of sight: the inner eye of the mind, the spiritual eye of grace, and even the physical pupil.

translit: eṉperuṅ kaḷippē yeṉperum poruḷē eṉperun tiṟalē yeṉperuñ ceyalē
translation: My great bliss, my great treasure, my great power, my great deed.
commentary: God is identified with the most essential aspects of personal experience. The divine is not sought as a separate goal, but is realized as one's own bliss, one's true wealth, one's capacity to act, and the very action itself.

translit: eṉperun tavamē eṉṟavap palaṉē eṉperuñ cukamē yeṉperum pēṟē
translation: My great penance and the very fruit of my penance, my great happiness, my great blessing.
commentary: Spiritual practice and its result are one and the same divine reality. Vallalar says that God is both the difficult discipline he undertakes (tavam, or penance) and the fruit that comes from it, showing there is no separation between the effort and the reward.

translit: eṉperu vāḻvē yeṉṟeṉvāḻ mutalē eṉperu vaḻakkē yeṉperuṅ kaṇakkē
translation: My great life! The very source of my life! My great justice! My great account!
commentary: The divine is both life itself and the source from which life springs. It is also the universal law of justice and the final measure of one's existence, a complete merging of the personal with the cosmic.

translit: eṉperu nalamē yeṉperuṅ kulamē eṉperu valamē yeṉperum pulamē
translation: My great good! My great lineage! My great strength! My great domain!
commentary: All that defines a person's identity and place in the world, their goodness, heritage, inner power, and sphere of influence, is here identified with the divine. The self expands to become one with God.

translit: eṉperu varamē yeṉperun taramē eṉperu neṟiyē yeṉperu nilaiyē
translation: My great boon! My great quality! My great path! My great state!
commentary: The grace received, the character it builds, the spiritual path taken, and the ultimate state of being attained are not separate stages. Vallalar sees them all as a single, unified expression of the divine.

translit: eṉperuṅ kuṇamē eṉperuṅ karuttē eṉperun tayavē yeṉperuṅ katiyē
translation: My great virtue! My great intention! My great compassion! My great refuge!
commentary: A person's inner world, their moral character, deepest intentions, and capacity for compassion, is not something they create on their own. It is the divine manifesting within them, offering both the virtue and the final refuge.

translit: eṉperum patiyē yeṉṉuyi riyalē eṉperu niṟaivē yeṉṟaṉi yaṟivē
translation: My great Lord! The very nature of my soul! My great fullness! My own unique knowledge
commentary: This is the ultimate statement of union. The divine is an external Lord to be worshipped and the very essence of the soul, the feeling of total fulfillment, and the direct, personal wisdom that comes from that unity.

translit: tōlelāṅ kuḻaintiṭac cūḻnaram paṉaittum mēlelāṅ kaṭṭavai viṭṭuviṭ ṭiyaṅkiṭa
translation: All the skin softens, and all the surrounding nerves, released from their bonds, move freely.
commentary: This begins a description of the body's complete transformation by grace. The process starts not with pain, but with a blissful release, as the very tissues of the body let go of their ordinary tension and structure.

translit: eṉpelā nekkunek kiyaliṭai nekiḻntiṭa meṉpuṭait tacaiyelā meyyuṟat taḷarntiṭa
translation: All the bones melt through and through, their structure softening; all the soft muscles relax completely.
commentary: The dissolving power of grace reaches even the most solid parts of the body. In Suddha Sanmarkkam this melting of the bones is not only a metaphor: it is the body's physical transformation as the Grace-Light descends.

translit: iratta maṉaittumuḷ ḷiṟukiṭac cukkilam urattiṭai pantit torutira ḷāyiṭa
translation: All the blood solidifies within; the seminal fluid binds in the chest, becoming a single mass.
commentary: In a process that defies normal biology, the body's frame softens while its vital energies do the opposite. The blood and seminal fluid are concentrated and drawn upward, suggesting their transmutation into a higher spiritual substance.

translit: maṭalelā mūḷai malarntiṭa vamutam uṭalelā mūṟṟeṭut tōṭi nirampiṭa
translation: All the lobes of the brain blossom; nectar springs forth, flows, and fills the entire body.
commentary: The transformation culminates as the brain, the seat of thought, opens like a flower. This blossoming releases a divine nectar, which then floods and reconstitutes the entire body with a substance of pure grace.

translit: oṇṇutal viyarttiṭa voḷimuka malarntiṭa taṇṇiya vuyirppiṉiṟ cāntan tatumpiṭa
translation: The radiant forehead sweats, the luminous face blossoms, and in the cool breath, serenity overflows.
commentary: These are the visible, outward signs of the profound inner change. The experience manifests as a radiant glow, a cool sweat of bliss, and a breath that carries an overwhelming sense of peace, showing the total saturation of the being with divine presence.

translit: uṇṇakai tōṟṟiṭa vurōmam poṭittiṭak kaṇṇiṉīr perukik kālvaḻin tōṭiṭa
translation: A smile appears from within and my body hair stands on end, as tears well in my eyes and stream down like a channel.
commentary: The body's response is one of overwhelming joy and awe. An inner smile, hair standing on end, and uncontrollable tears are classic signs of spiritual ecstasy and satchitananda, showing a state where the devotee is completely overcome by the divine, blissful presence.

translit: vāytuṭit talaṟiṭa vaḷarcevit tuṇaikaḷiṟ kūyicaip poṟiyelāṅ kummeṉak koṭṭiṭa
translation: My mouth trembles and cries out, as all the subtle, humming sounds pour into my ears with a roar.
commentary: The experience intensifies, overwhelming the senses. The devotee cries out involuntarily, while the inner ear is filled with a roaring sound, the culmination of all subtle cosmic vibrations. This is the sound of the divine reality making itself known directly.

translit: meyyelāṅ kuḷirntiṭa meṉmār pacaintiṭak kaiyelāṅ kuvintiṭak kālelāñ culaviṭa
translation: My whole body grows cool and my tender chest heaves, as my hands join together and my feet circle about.
commentary: The body moves in spontaneous devotion. The experience is cooling, a sign of its divine nature, distinct from worldly heat or passion. The hands naturally come together in reverence, and the feet begin to move in a dance of joy, as if orbiting the divine center.

translit: maṉaṅkaṉin turukiṭa matiniṟain toḷirntiṭa iṉampeṟu citta miyaintu kaḷittiṭa
translation: My mind ripens and melts and my intellect becomes full and luminous, as my consciousness, having found its kin, unites and rejoices.
commentary: The inner faculties are transformed by this experience. The analytical mind (manam) softens and melts, while the intellect (mati) becomes clear and bright. Consciousness itself (siddham) feels a profound sense of homecoming, as if it has finally found and merged with its own true source.

translit: akaṅkāra māṅkāṅ katikarip pamaintiṭac cakaṅkāṇa vuḷḷan taḻaittu malarntiṭa
translation: The excesses of the ego subside everywhere, as my heart flourishes and blossoms for all the world to see.
commentary: As the experience deepens, the excess of the ego (agangāram) subsides. With the pride of the separate self quieted, the heart blossoms openly with love, for all the world to see.

translit: aṟivuru vaṉaittu māṉanta māyiṭap poṟiyuṟu māṉmataṟ pōtamum pōyiṭat
translation: As all forms of consciousness become bliss, and the awareness of the sense-bound soul and the ego itself disappear,
commentary: In this state of transformation, the boundary between awareness and joy dissolves. To be conscious is to be blissful. As this happens, the old, limited identities, like the feeling of being a physical body with senses or a separate egoic personality, simply fall away.

translit: tattuva maṉaittun tāmoruṅ koḻintiṭac cattuva moṉṟē taṉittuniṉ ṟōṅkiṭa
translation: As all the tattvas are completely cleared away, and sattva alone remains, standing and flourishing,
commentary: The tattvas are the fundamental building blocks of reality, the cosmic principles that create the universe and the individual. Vallalar says that in the ultimate experience, this entire complex structure is swept away. All that remains is sattva: pure existence, goodness, and luminosity, standing alone and radiant.

translit: ulakelām viṭaya muḷavelā maṟaintiṭa alakilā varuḷi ṉācaimēṟ poṅkiṭa
translation: As all worlds and all the sense objects within them disappear, and longing for boundless grace surges upward,
commentary: The inward journey requires a withdrawal of attention from the outer world. As the world of sense objects (viṭayam) fades, the energy previously spent on it is redirected. It becomes a powerful, surging desire for one thing only: the boundless grace of God.

translit: eṉṉuḷat teḻuntuyi rellā malarntiṭa eṉṉuḷat tōṅkiya eṉṟaṉi yaṉpē
translation: As you rise in my heart and cause all souls to blossom, O my unique Love that has flourished within my soul!
commentary: Here, Vallalar addresses God as the Love that has grown within his own heart. He sees that this divine presence is not for his benefit alone. When God rises within one person, the effect is universal, causing all souls everywhere to blossom and awaken. Personal liberation and universal upliftment are one and the same.

translit: poṉṉaṭi kaṇṭaruṭ puttamu tuṇavē eṉṉuḷat teḻunta veṉṉuṭai yaṉpē
translation: O my own Love, you who arose in my heart so that I could see the golden feet and consume the fresh nectar of grace
commentary: The love for God is not something we manufacture ourselves; it is a gift that arises from within. Vallalar recognizes that this love is the very thing that enables him to perceive the divine presence (symbolized by the "golden feet") and receive the life-giving nectar of grace. Love is the means, the path, and the key.

translit: taṉṉaiyē yeṉakkut tantaru ḷoḷiyāl eṉṉaivē titta eṉṟaṉi yaṉpē
translation: My unique Love, who gave Himself to me and transmuted me with the light of grace.
commentary: Divine grace is not a gift given from a distance; it is a total self-giving that fundamentally changes the recipient. The "light of grace" acts like an alchemical agent, transmuting the ordinary self into a divine nature.

translit: eṉṉuḷē yarumpi yeṉṉuḷē malarntu eṉṉuḷē virinta eṉṉuṭai yaṉpē
translation: My own Love, who budded, blossomed, and expanded all within me.
commentary: The awakening of Love is described as an organic process unfolding entirely within the self. Like a flower, it buds, blossoms, and expands, suggesting a natural and internal growth rather than an external imposition.

translit: eṉṉuḷē viḷaṅki yeṉṉuḷē paḻuttu eṉṉuḷē kaṉinta veṉṉuṭai yaṉpē
translation: My own Love, who manifested, ripened, and became perfectly sweet all within me.
commentary: Continuing the metaphor of organic growth, divine Love is now likened to a fruit. It appears, ripens over time, and achieves perfect sweetness, all within the landscape of his own being.

translit: taṉṉuḷē niṟaivuṟu taramelā maḷittē eṉṉuḷē niṟainta eṉṟaṉi yaṉpē
translation: My unique Love, who bestowed all the qualities complete within Himself and filled me.
commentary: Being filled with God means receiving God's own qualities. The divine Love fills the soul by bestowing all the perfections and completeness that are inherent to God's own nature.

translit: tuṉpuḷa vaṉaittun tolaitteṉa turuvai yiṉpuṟu vākkiya eṉṉuṭai yaṉpē
translation: My own Love, who destroyed all suffering and made my form into a form of bliss.
commentary: This divine Love brings an end to all suffering. It goes further by transforming his very physical form (uruvu) into an embodiment of bliss, making his body a source and expression of joy.

translit: poṉṉuṭam peṉakkup poruntiṭum poruṭṭā eṉṉuḷaṅ kalanta eṉṟaṉi yaṉpē
translation: My singular love, who mingled with my heart so that a golden body would become mine.
commentary: The union with divine Love has a physical outcome: the creation of a poṉ uṭampu, or 'golden body'. This is a central, tangible goal in Vallalar's path, where spiritual realization leads to the body's transformation into an immortal, light-filled form.

translit: taṉvaca mākit tatumpimēṟ poṅki eṉvacaṅ kaṭanta eṉṉuṭai yaṉpē
translation: My own love, who became self-possessed, brimmed over and surged up, surpassing my control.
commentary: The experience of divine love is not something the individual can create or manage. It is an overwhelming force that rises on its own, taking over completely and moving beyond the limits of personal will and control.

translit: taṉṉuḷē poṅkiya taṇṇamu tuṇavē eṉṉuḷē poṅkiya eṉṟaṉi yaṉpē
translation: My singular love, who welled up within me to consume the cool ambrosia that surged from within yourself.
commentary: A beautiful cycle of bliss is described here, all happening within the devotee. The divine is the source of a spiritual nectar, and it is also the one who enjoys that nectar. The soul becomes the sacred space where God provides and partakes in his own feast.

translit: aruḷoḷi viḷaṅkiṭa vāṇava meṉumōr iruḷaṟa veṉṉuḷat tēṟṟiya viḷakkē
translation: The lamp lit in my heart to completely dispel the darkness called Āṇavam, allowing the light of grace to shine.
commentary: The divine presence acts like a lamp inside the heart. Its light has a specific function: to destroy āṇavam, the primal ignorance or ego-conceit that makes us feel separate from God. Once this core darkness is gone, the light of grace can finally shine through.

translit: tuṉpuṟu tattuvat turicelā nīkkinal liṉpuṟa veṉṉuḷat tēṟṟiya viḷakkē
translation: The lamp lit in my heart, who removed all the impurities of the sorrow-inducing tattvas so that I could attain good bliss.
commentary: The tattvas are the basic components of our mind and body, the building blocks of our experience. In their ordinary state, they cause suffering. The divine light purifies these very elements, transforming the human constitution from a machine that produces sorrow into one that experiences pure bliss.

translit: mayalaṟa vaḻiyā vāḻvumēṉ mēlum iyaluṟa veṉṉuḷat tēṟṟiya viḷakkē
translation: The Lamp lit within my heart, making an imperishable life, free from delusion, increasingly attainable.
commentary: This divine lamp does more than offer a feeling of peace; it fundamentally changes what is possible for a human being. It opens the path to an imperishable life, a state of existence free from both mental delusion and physical decay, making it a tangible goal rather than a distant dream.

translit: iṭuveḷi yaṉaittu miyaloḷi viḷaṅkiṭa naṭuveḷi naṭuvē nāṭṭiya viḷakkē
translation: The Lamp planted in the very center of the middle expanse, causing all confined spaces to shine with innate light.
commentary: The divine light is more than inside him; it is the central point of a universal spiritual reality, the "middle expanse." From this center, it radiates outward, illuminating every "confined space", meaning every individual soul and every limited part of creation, filling them with their own true, innate light.

translit: karuveḷi yaṉaittuṅ katiroḷi viḷaṅkiṭa uruveḷi naṭuvē yoḷirtaru viḷakkē
translation: The Lamp that shines in the center of the expanse of form, making all the causal expanses shine with radiant light.
commentary: God's light is present at the heart of the visible, physical world (the "expanse of form"). Yet its source and effect are deeper, illuminating the "causal expanses," the formless, unmanifested realms from which all creation emerges. This light connects the seen with the unseen, the effect with its ultimate cause.

translit: tēṟṟiya vētat tirumuṭi viḷaṅkiṭa ēṟṟiya ñāṉa viyaloḷi viḷakkē
translation: The Lamp of the innate light of wisdom, lit so that the sacred pinnacle of the clarified Vedas shines brightly.
commentary: The Vedas are revered scriptures, but their highest truths can be obscure. The divine light is itself Jnana, or direct spiritual wisdom, and this inner experience illuminates the ultimate meaning of the Vedas, revealing the core truth that scriptures can only point towards.

translit: ākama muṭimē laruḷoḷi viḷaṅkiṭa vēkama taṟavē viḷaṅkoḷi viḷakkē
translation: The resplendent Lamp that shines to completely end all agitation, making the light of grace illuminate the pinnacle of the Agamas.
commentary: Like the Vedas, the Agamas are sacred texts containing profound teachings. The divine light has two effects here: it ends all inner mental and emotional agitation (vēkam), bringing perfect stillness, and it reveals the highest purpose of the Agamas, which is the experience of divine grace. True understanding of scripture comes from inner peace, more than intellectual study.

translit: āriyar vaḻuttiya varuṇilai yaṉāti kāriyam viḷakkumōr kāraṇa viḷakkē
translation: The Causal Lamp that illuminates the beginningless effect and the state of grace praised by the wise.
commentary: The divine light is the ultimate cause of everything. It illuminates the highest state a soul can achieve, a destination so profound that it has been praised by the wise throughout history.

translit: taṇṇiya vamutē tanteṉa tuḷattē puṇṇiyam palitta pūraṇa matiyē
translation: The cool nectar given to me, the Full Moon that has ripened in my heart as my good deeds bore fruit.
commentary: The divine is a distant light and an intimate, personal experience. Vallalar feels it inside himself as a cooling nectar, like a full moon in his heart, which he sees as the natural result of his past good deeds (puṇṇiyam).

translit: uytara vamuta mutaviyeṉ ṉuḷattē ceytavam palitta tiruvaḷar matiyē
translation: The nectar given for my salvation, the Grace-filled Moon that has ripened in my heart where the penance I performed bore fruit.
commentary: This inner experience of grace is the very goal of spiritual effort. The nectar that grants salvation arises from the ripening of tavam, which is intense spiritual discipline and self-purification.

translit: patiyelān taḻaikkap patampeṟu mamuta nitiyelā maḷitta niṟaitiru matiyē
translation: The perfect, Grace-filled Moon that gives all the treasures of nectar which grant the supreme state, so that all realms may flourish.
commentary: The grace one receives is not meant for that person alone. It is an endless treasure that grants the supreme state (patam) to the individual while also pouring out to nourish and uplift all realms and all beings.

translit: pāleṉat taṇkatir parappiyeñ ñāṉṟu mēlveḷi viḷaṅka viḷaṅkiya matiyē
translation: The luminous Moon that forever spreads its cool rays like milk, making the supreme space radiant.
commentary: The divine presence is gentle, constant, and nourishing, like cool moonbeams or pure milk. It spreads everywhere, illuminating the supreme space (mēlveḷi), the highest dimension of pure consciousness.

translit: uyaṅkiya uḷḷamu muyirun taḻaittiṭa vayaṅkiya karuṇai maḻaipoḻi maḻaiyē
translation: O Cloud pouring a rain of resplendent grace, so that my languishing heart and soul may flourish.
commentary: The central metaphor now shifts from the moon to a raincloud. Grace is a revitalizing rain that falls upon a "languishing" heart and soul, bringing life back to what was withered and dry.

translit: eṉṉaiyum paṇikoṇ ṭeṉṉuḷē nirampa maṉṉiya karuṇai maḻaipoḻi maḻaiyē
translation: O Cloud pouring a rain of abiding grace, accepting even me into Your service and filling me completely within.
commentary: The rain of grace has a dual effect: it signifies divine acceptance, welcoming even a humble seeker into God's service, and it transforms the person from within by filling them completely.

translit: uḷaṅkoḷu meṉakkē yuvakaimēṟ poṅki vaḷaṅkoḷak karuṇai maḻaipoḻi maḻaiyē
translation: O Cloud pouring a rain of grace, that I, whose heart You possess, may receive abundance as joy overflows.
commentary: The fruit of surrender: Because God already possesses his heart, the rain of grace results in an overflowing joy and a profound inner abundance.

translit: nalantara vuṭaluyir nallaṟi veṉakkē malarntiṭak karuṇai maḻaipoḻi maḻaiyē
translation: O Cloud pouring a rain of grace, so that for my well-being, my body, soul, and true wisdom may blossom.
commentary: Vallalar's vision is holistic, seeking well-being for the entire person. He asks that grace make his body (uṭal), soul (uyir), and true wisdom (nallaṟivu) all blossom together.

translit: tūymaiyā leṉatu turicelā nīkkinal vāymaiyāṟ karuṇai maḻaipoḻi maḻaiyē
translation: O Cloud, who by Your purity remove all my impurities, and by Your true reality pour a rain of grace
commentary: God's very nature is the agent of transformation. It is by God's own purity that the seeker's flaws are washed away, and by God's own truth that the rain of grace is poured out.

translit: vemmala viravatu viṭitaru ṇantaṉiṟ cemmaiyi lutittuḷan tikaḻntaceñ cuṭarē
translation: O Red Flame, who rose in perfection and shone in my heart at the dawn that ended the night of harsh malam
commentary: The arrival of divine consciousness is like a sunrise within the heart, ending the long, dark night of malam, the accumulated spiritual impurity that obscures the soul's true nature.

translit: tiraiyelān tavirttuc cevviyuṟ ṟāṅkē varaiyelām viḷaṅka vayaṅkuceñ cuṭarē
translation: O shining Red Flame, who removed all the veils and, attaining perfection right there, made all the mountains luminous!
commentary: This divine light removes all the inner veils that prevent us from perceiving reality clearly. Once those obstructions are gone, the light illumines our entire inner world, which Vallalar describes as mountains.

translit: alakilāt talaivarka ḷaracucey tattuva ulakelām viḷaṅka vōṅkuceñ cuṭarē
translation: O lofty Red Flame, who makes luminous all the worlds of the tattvas, which are ruled by countless lords!
commentary: The divine light is the source of all reality. It illuminates the tattvas (the fundamental principles or building blocks of the cosmos), which are themselves governed by countless divine beings.

translit: muṉṉuṟu malaviruḷ muḻuvatu nīkkiyē eṉṉuḷa varaimē leḻuntaceñ cuṭarē
translation: O Red Flame, who completely dispelled the preceding darkness of malam and rose upon the mountain of my heart!
commentary: This experience of enlightenment is intensely personal. The divine light rises like a sun upon the "mountain of my heart," completely clearing away the darkness of past impurity (malam).

translit: ātiyu naṭuvuṭa ṉantamuṅ kaṭanta jōtiyā yeṉṉuḷañ cūḻntameyc cuṭarē
translation: O True Flame, who, as the Jothi that transcends beginning, middle, and end, has enveloped my heart
commentary: The flame within the heart is identified as the ultimate reality, the divine Jothi or Light, which is eternal and exists beyond time's limits of beginning, middle, and end. This infinite reality has completely surrounded and filled his personal consciousness.

translit: uḷḷoḷi yōṅkiṭa vuyiroḷi viḷaṅkiṭa veḷḷoḷi kāṭṭiya meyyaruṭ kaṉalē
translation: O true grace-flame that showed the white light, causing the inner light to rise and the light of the soul to shine forth!
commentary: God's grace, the "true grace-flame," acts as a catalyst. By revealing its own great light, it awakens and intensifies the light that is already present within the soul, causing both our inner awareness and the soul's inherent luminosity to shine fully.

translit: nalaṅkoḷap purintiṭu ñāṉayā kattiṭai valañcuḻit teḻuntu vaḷarntameyk kaṉalē
translation: O true flame that rose swirling clockwise and grew within the wisdom-sacrifice performed for the attainment of good!
commentary: A jnana yagam is a "wisdom-sacrifice," but for Vallalar this is not an external fire ritual. It is the inner process of offering one's own ego and ignorance to the flame of divine wisdom. The flame rising in a clockwise direction is an auspicious sign, indicating this inner worship is accepted and blessed.

translit: vētamu mākama virivum parampara nātamuṅ kaṭanta ñāṉameyk kaṉalē
translation: O true flame of wisdom that has transcended the Vedas, the expanse of the Agamas, and the primordial sound!
commentary: The Vedas and Agamas are the foundational scriptures of Hinduism, and the primordial sound (nadam) is considered the source of all creation. Vallalar declares that the direct experience of God as a flame of wisdom goes beyond all of them. For him, lived experience of the divine is the ultimate authority, higher than any text or cosmic principle.

translit: eṇṇiya veṇṇiya vellāntara veṉuḷ naṇṇiya puṇṇiya ñāṉameyk kaṉalē
translation: O sacred, true flame of wisdom that entered me to give all that I have ever imagined!
commentary: This inner flame is more than for illumination; it is the source of all fulfillment. Vallalar feels that its presence within him is the very power that can grant every aspiration he has ever conceived.

translit: valamuṟu cuttacaṉ mārkka nilaipeṟu nalamelā maḷitta ñāṉameyk kaṉalē
translation: O true flame of wisdom that bestowed all the goodness obtained in the state of the mighty Suddha Sanmarkkam
commentary: Suddha Sanmarkkam is the "True Path of Purity," the universal spiritual way of life that Vallalar taught. He sees this inner flame of wisdom as the very power that delivers all the blessings and ultimate goals of that path, including compassion, wisdom, and the deathless life.

translit: iravoṭu pakalilā viyalpotu naṭamiṭu paramavē tāntap paramparañ cuṭarē
translation: Supreme, transcendent flame of the highest Vedanta, performing the dance in the natural common space that is without night and day.
commentary: God's creative activity is a constant dance, happening in a space beyond all dualities like night and day. Vallalar identifies this dancing flame with the ultimate reality sought by Vedanta, a major school of Indian philosophy focused on the nature of God and existence.

translit: varaniṟai potuviṭai vaḷartiru naṭampuri paramacit tāntap patiparañ cuṭarē
translation: Supreme Lord, transcendent flame of the highest Siddhanta, performing the flourishing sacred dance in the common space filled with grace.
commentary: The same divine flame is also the supreme Lord described in Siddhanta, another great philosophical tradition. By invoking both Vedanta and Siddhanta in consecutive verses, Vallalar suggests they both point to the same ultimate reality, which he experiences as a dance of grace in a universal space.

translit: camaraca cattiyac capaiyi ṉaṭampuri camaraca cattiyat taṟcuyañ cuṭarē
translation: Self-existent flame of harmonious truth, dancing in the hall of harmonious truth.
commentary: The ultimate reality is a state of samarasa sattiyam, or harmonious truth. This truth is self-existent, and it is both the space where the divine dance happens and the dancer itself. The divine is the stage, the actor, and the action, all in one state of perfect harmony.

translit: capaiyeṉa tuḷameṉat tāṉamarn teṉakkē apaya maḷittatō raruṭperuñ jōti
translation: The Supreme Grace-Light that took my heart as its hall, settled there, and granted me refuge.
commentary: The vast, cosmic hall of the divine dance becomes intensely personal. That universal space of God's presence can be found within one's own heart, offering intimate safety and refuge (abayam).

translit: maruḷelān tavirttu varamelāṅ koṭuttē aruḷamu taruttiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: The Supreme Grace-Light that dispelled all delusion, granted all boons, and fed me the nectar of grace.
commentary: When the Supreme Grace-Light settles in the heart, it transforms experience completely. It removes the mental fog of delusion, bestows the blessings of spiritual clarity, and nourishes the soul with the sweet, life-giving experience of grace.

translit: vāḻiniṉ pēraruḷ vāḻiniṉ peruñcīr āḻiyoṉ ṟaḷitta varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Hail to Your great grace, hail to Your great glory, O Vast Grace-Light, who bestowed the one sphere of command.
commentary: This is a cry of praise and gratitude. The "one sphere of command" (āḻi) refers to the spiritual authority and sovereignty granted to the devotee by the Grace-Light, which is a direct result of its inner presence.

translit: eṉṉaiyum poruḷeṉa veṇṇiyeṉ ṉuḷattē aṉṉaiyu mappaṉu mākivīṟ ṟiruntu
translation: Considering even me a being of worth, becoming my mother and father, and residing majestically in my heart,
commentary: Vallalar expresses profound humility and wonder, feeling that even he was seen as worthy by the divine. In these connected verses (781-784), he explains that God's presence is not abstract, but takes on the intimate, loving roles of both mother and father within his own heart.

translit: ulakiyal ciṟitu muḷampiṭi yāvakai alakilpē raruḷā laṟivatu viḷakkic
translation: illuminating knowledge through Your measureless great grace, so that my mind would not cling in the slightest to worldly ways,
commentary: True spiritual knowledge is a gift of grace, not an achievement of the intellect. This divine illumination frees the mind from its attachment to worldly life (ulakiyal), which is seen as a source of distraction and suffering.

translit: ciṟuneṟi cellāt tiṟaṉaḷit taḻiyā tuṟuneṟi yuṇarccitan toḷiyuṟap purintu
translation: granting me the strength not to walk the lesser path, giving me the realization of the imperishable, true path, and making me radiant with light,
commentary: Grace provides the moral and spiritual strength to reject lesser paths (ciṟu neṟi), which are temporary and lead to dead ends. It reveals the one true, eternal path (uṟu neṟi) and fills the person who walks it with an inner light and purity.

translit: cākāk kalviyiṉ ṟaramelā muṇarttic cākā varattaiyun tantumēṉ mēlum
translation: teaching me all the principles of the deathless education, and giving me the boon of deathlessness, again and again,
commentary: The highest knowledge grace can impart is the "deathless education" (sākāk kalvi), the practical science of overcoming physical death itself. Vallalar states that this knowledge, and the resulting boon (varam) of immortality, was given to him directly and repeatedly by the divine.

translit: aṉpaiyum viḷaivit taruṭpē roḷiyāl iṉpaiyu niṟaivit teṉṉaiyu niṉṉaiyum
translation: You cultivated love, filled me with bliss through your great light of grace, and took me and you,
commentary: The journey toward God begins with God's own action within the soul. Grace actively cultivates love and fills the person with a bliss that is a direct experience of the divine light, preparing them for the ultimate union.

translit: ōruru vākkiyā ṉuṉṉiya paṭiyelāñ cīruṟac ceytuyirt tiṟampeṟa vaḻiyā
translation: made us into one form, perfectly accomplished all that I intended, and so that my soul would attain its power,
commentary: The ultimate goal: the soul and God merging into a single form. In this state of perfect union, the individual's intentions are fulfilled effortlessly because they have become one with the divine will.

translit: aruḷamu taḷittaṉai yaruṇilai yēṟṟiṉai aruḷaṟi vaḷittaṉai yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: You gave the imperishable nectar of grace. You raised me to the state of grace. You granted me the wisdom of grace, O Arutperunjothi.
commentary: Grace is experienced in three ways: as a nourishing nectar that gives life, as an elevated state of consciousness, and as a profound wisdom that sees things as they truly are. It is the total gift of Arutperunjothi (the Vast Grace-Light).

translit: velkaniṉ pēraruḷ velkaniṉ peruñcīr alkaliṉ ṟōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Victory to your supreme grace! Victory to your great glory! O Arutperunjothi, risen high without ever diminishing.
commentary: After describing his personal experience of transformation, Vallalar erupts in a cry of pure praise. The victory belongs to grace, the eternal and inexhaustible light of God that never fades.

translit: ulakuyirt tiraḷelā moḷineṟi peṟṟiṭa ilakumain toḻilaiyum yāṉceyat tantaṉai
translation: So that all the multitudes of life in the world may attain the path of light, you have given me the power to perform the five luminous cosmic functions.
commentary: This is an extraordinary statement of purpose. The ultimate fruit of union with God is not personal bliss, but receiving the divine power to help all other beings. Vallalar states that grace has empowered him to perform the five cosmic functions (creation, sustenance, dissolution, obscuration, and grace) traditionally associated only with God, so he can guide every soul to the path of light.

translit: pōṟṟiniṉ pēraruḷ pōṟṟiniṉ peruñcīr āṟṟali ṉōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Praise to Your great grace, praise to Your great majesty, O Arutperunjothi supreme in power.
commentary: This refrain shifts from the cry of "Victory" to one of "Praise." It expresses deep reverence for the divine grace and majesty embodied in the Arutperunjothi (Vast Grace-Light), acknowledging it as the source of all power.

translit: mūvarun tēvaru muttaruñ cittarum yāvarum peṟṟiṭā viyaleṉak kaḷittaṉai
translation: You have granted me the state that the Trinity, the gods, the liberated, the perfected masters, and all others could not attain.
commentary: The state Vallalar has received stands above all known spiritual goals. He claims it is a condition that even the great gods of the Hindu trinity, other celestial beings, and perfected sages have not reached, suggesting the path he teaches leads to a unique and supreme form of union with God.

translit: pōṟṟiniṉ pēraruḷ pōṟṟiniṉ peruñcīr āṟṟali ṉōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Praise to Your great grace, praise to Your great majesty, O Arutperunjothi, supreme in power.
commentary: Repeating the refrain of praise emphasizes that these extraordinary gifts do not come from the self, but from the divine. Each profound realization is immediately followed by a return to adoration and humility before the source, the Arutperunjothi.

translit: cittika ḷaṉaittaiyun teḷivit teṉakkē cattiya nilaitaṉait tayaviṉiṟ ṟantaṉai
translation: You made the nature of all siddhis clear to me, and out of Your kindness, You gave me the very state of Truth.
commentary: Spiritual practice can sometimes result in siddhis, or supernatural powers. Instead of just granting him these powers, Vallalar says God gave him something more valuable: a clear understanding of their nature. More importantly, he was given the "state of Truth" itself, showing that ultimate reality is a far greater prize than any extraordinary ability.

translit: pōṟṟiniṉ pēraruḷ pōṟṟiniṉ peruñcīr āṟṟali ṉōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Praise to Your great grace, praise to Your great majesty, O Arutperunjothi, supreme in power.
commentary: The repetition of this line of praise serves as a constant reminder. All the states and powers described are not personal achievements but gifts of grace from the one supreme, powerful light.

translit: ulakiṉi luyirkaḷuk kuṟumiṭai yūṟelām vilakanī yaṭaintu vilakkuka makiḻka
translation: Go and remove all the hindrances that beset the lives in this world so they are dispelled, and rejoice,
commentary: This is not a prayer to God but God's command to Vallalar: go into the world and remove the suffering and hindrances of all living beings. Universal compassion and service are the mandate.

translit: cuttacaṉ mārkka cukanilai peṟuka uttama ṉākuka vōṅkuka veṉṟaṉai
translation: You who told me: "Attain the blissful state of Suddha Sanmarkkam. Become a perfected one. Flourish."
commentary: The spiritual path is presented here as a direct command from God. The instruction is to achieve the blissful state of Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path), become a perfected being, and flourish. This transforms the quest from a human aspiration into a divine mandate.

translit: pōṟṟiniṉ pēraruḷ pōṟṟiniṉ peruñcīr āṟṟali ṉōṅkiya varuṭperuñ jōti
translation: Praise to your great grace, praise to your great glory, O Arutperunjothi, supreme in power.
commentary: The repetition of this verse acts as a powerful refrain. In devotional poetry, such repetition is more than for emphasis; it is a way to build spiritual feeling, deepening the worshipper's focus on the awesome grace and power of Arutperunjothi (the Vast Grace-Light).

translit: aruṭperuñ jōti yaruṭperuñ jōti aruṭperuñ jōti yaruṭperuñ jōti
translation: Vast Grace-Light, Vast Grace-Light. Vast Grace-Light, Vast Grace-Light.
commentary: The poem gloriously culminates in this simple, profound chant. All description and praise resolve into the direct repetition of the divine name, Arutperunjothi.
The Arutperunjothi Agaval is complete
May all living beings live happily forever! – Vallalar

glossary.def: Impurity. For Vallalar, this refers to the layers of karma and ignorance that cover the soul, which the Grace-Light actively removes.
The inner self or interior space. Vallalar maps reality into distinct layers, emphasizing that the Jothi structures our internal reality just as it does the external universe.
The letter 'A'. As the first letter of the alphabet, it symbolizes the primal origin of all things. Vallalar identifies the divine Jothi as this fundamental source.
Agamas. The scriptures of temple worship and doctrine. Vallalar says their truth is known by grace, not by reading.
Agaval. A Tamil verse form of long, flowing lines. The Arutperunjothi Agaval, Vallalar's hymn of 1,596 lines, belongs to the Sixth Thirumurai.
Ambalam. The hall or open stage where God dances. It is the hall at Chidambaram and, within, the space of consciousness where God is known.
Ambrosia, nectar. Vallalar's word for the sweetness of grace, tasted within, which brings deathless life.
Bliss, Ananda. The joy of union with God.
Anava. The root impurity of the ego, the "I-ness" that veils the soul. The first of the three impurities (malam).
The universe, the macrocosm. Vallalar sees the same Light filling the countless universes (aṇṭam) and the human body (piṇṭam).
Traditionally a name for Brahmins. Vallalar gives it its root meaning: the gracious ones whose nature is coolness and compassion toward all life, whatever their birth.
Anubhavam. Direct personal experience. Vallalar teaches that true spiritual knowledge is not learned from books but is gained only through one's own unmediated experience of divine Grace.
Refuge or fearlessness. The state of absolute security granted by the Grace-Light, which personally assures the soul of its protection from all suffering.
Virtue, righteous action. For Vallalar its heart is compassion: feeding the hungry and relieving the suffering of every living being.
A name for the Vedas. Vallalar teaches that the Vast Grace-Light is the living source and culmination of their wisdom.
Consciousness or wisdom. For Vallalar, this is not learned knowledge but a direct awareness of truth gifted by grace.
Grace. The active, compassionate power of God that frees the soul and transforms it. For Vallalar grace is received through compassion for all life.
Arutperunjothi. The Vast Grace-Light. Vallalar's name for the ultimate, compassionate divine reality, the one infinite Light of grace from which everything comes.
The deathless education: the knowledge, given by grace, of the life that does not end in death.
The waking state, the first of the states of consciousness.
Salai, the hall or house. Here the Sathya Dharma Salai, the free kitchen at Vadalur.
Samarasam: perfect harmony, equality of all. Part of the full name of Vallalar's path, Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam.
Religion as an organized creed. Vallalar declares sectarian religions false, calling people to the universal path of light.
Sanmarkkam. The true path. Vallalar's name for the way of grace, compassion and direct knowledge of God, open to every living being.
Satguru, the true teacher. In Vallalar's path, the true Guru is ultimately God, the Vast Grace-Light, who manifests as an inner guide teaching the soul directly.
Sat. Being or Existence. Vallalar identifies the divine as the fundamental reality that is eternal and fills everything.
Saktas. Beings of power, perfected masters and celestial beings whose abilities come from the divine Jothi.
Sakti. Divine power or energy, often personified as a goddess. In Vallalar's teaching, the active, creative force of the cosmos, directed by the Vast Grace-Light.
Chit Sabhai, the Hall of Consciousness. The space of pure consciousness where God's dance of grace is known; outwardly, the hall at Chidambaram.
Chit. Consciousness or pure awareness. The active, all-creating intelligence of the one ultimate substance, which Vallalar experiences as divine light.
Chidambaram. A sacred temple town in Tamil Nadu, meaning "expanse of consciousness." Vallalar internalizes it as the inner space within the soul where divine wisdom is revealed.
Cittam. Consciousness or mind-stuff. For Vallalar, the ultimate spiritual goal involves the divine consciousness completely replacing and becoming one's own.
Siddhanta. The philosophical tradition of Saivism. Vallalar presents the experience of the Jothi as the ultimate fulfillment of its goal.
Siddha. Perfected masters of the Tamil tradition, known for their esoteric powers and pursuit of physical immortality, which Vallalar says are byproducts of grace.
Siddhi. Spiritual powers or perfections. For Vallalar, these are not goals in themselves but gifts of grace, the greatest being the transformation into an immortal body of light.
Jeevakarunyam. Compassion for all living beings. For Vallalar this active compassion, above all feeding the hungry, is the door to the grace of the Jothi.
Siva. The supreme divine reality, characterized by pure goodness, bliss, and grace for all beings. For Vallalar, this formless reality is identical to the Vast Grace-Light.
Suddha, purity. The soul's original, flawless state, which is revealed when all impurities are removed by divine grace.
Jothi, the divine Light. For Vallalar, it is not physical light but the conscious, compassionate form of God experienced directly within.
Kalai. A subtle division of power, aspect of knowledge, or cosmic principle. Vallalar sees the universe as structured by innumerable kalais, all expressions of the Grace-Light.
Kalantam. The state beyond subtle cosmic energies. It marks a high stage of spiritual ascent where the soul transcends limiting principles of consciousness.
Karma. The universal law of action and consequence that binds beings to the cycle of birth. For Vallalar, the Jothi’s grace completely removes the accumulated darkness of karma.
Murder. For Vallalar, this means the murder of any living being, not only of humans. It is the ultimate violation of compassion and an absolute barrier to grace.
Guru. Spiritual teacher. Vallalar identifies God himself as the ultimate Guru who teaches the soul directly from within.
Impurity. The innate spiritual dirt, such as ego (anava) and karma, that clouds the soul. Vallalar sees the divine light as the only agent that can completely burn it away.
Mantra. A sacred utterance. For Vallalar, the ultimate reality of the Grace-Light is itself the supreme mantra, surpassing all scriptural formulas.
Maya. Illusion, the cosmic power of delusion that makes the unreal appear real and projects the material world. The Grace-Light utterly destroys its bewildering effects.
Mukti, liberation. Vallalar says it is not the end but the means that comes before the true state, siddhi: deathless life in grace.
Natham or Nada. Primordial sound or subtle, unstruck vibration from which all creation emerges.
Nadantam. The state beyond primal sound. This is a supreme point of inner experience where Vallalar places the divine Jothi's dance.
Jnana. Divine or spiritual wisdom. For Vallalar, this is not intellectual learning but a direct, experiential knowledge bestowed by grace.
Omkara or Om. The sacred syllable and primordial sound vibration from which creation unfolds, containing its own divine energies.
Pasam. The bond or fetter. The tethers of ego, karma, and illusion that bind the soul and cause suffering.
Pasu. The individual soul. Inherently conscious but bound by impurities and limitations, it is guided to liberation by the Guru.
Parai. The Supreme Power, the dynamic feminine aspect of the Divine. Vallalar identifies this active, creative power with the Grace-Light itself.
Paramparam. The transcendent or the supreme. The divine reality as it exists beyond all worlds and manifestations.
Paraparam. The supreme that is both beyond and here. It describes God as the reality that is both transcendent and immanently present within the body.
Pati. The Lord or Master. A classic term for God, which Vallalar identifies as the immanent Vast Grace-Light, the ultimate authority and sovereign of all existence.
The physical body, viewed as a microcosm. Vallalar presents the body as a miniature universe that perfectly mirrors the entire cosmos (aṇṭam).
Brahman. The ultimate, absolute reality. Vallalar teaches that this formless ground of being is the same as the compassionate Vast Grace-Light.
Brahma. The Hindu god of creation. Vallalar sees him as a cosmic agent appointed by and subordinate to the Vast Grace-Light.
The exterior or outer realm. This refers to the objective, physical world that can be perceived by the senses, which is structured by the Grace-Light.
Satchidananda. Being-Consciousness-Bliss. A classic term for the nature of the Absolute, which Vallalar uses to describe the inherent quality of the divine expanse.
Tantra. The esoteric traditions and texts. Vallalar places direct experience of the divine light above their systems.
Tattva. A fundamental principle or element of existence. These are the cosmic building blocks of creation, which the soul must see beyond to realize God.
Spiritual discipline, austerity. Vallalar redefines it: not harsh penance, but the loving practice of Jeevakarunyam and constant remembrance of God.
Turiya. The "fourth" state of consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. Vallalar says the divine Jothi resides in a space even higher than this.
Rudra. The Hindu god of dissolution. For Vallalar, he is a deity of cosmic destruction who is ultimately governed and empowered by the Grace-Light.
Vallalar, "the Great Giver": the name by which Ramalinga Adigal (1823–1874), the Tamil saint and poet who taught Suddha Sanmarkkam and wrote the Arutperunjothi Agaval, is lovingly known.
Vedas. The most ancient and foundational scriptures of Hinduism. Vallalar respects them but states the divine Jothi is the supreme reality they can only point toward.
Vedanta. The philosophical culmination of the Vedas. For Vallalar, direct experience of the Jothi is the final truth that transcends even this high philosophy.
Vishnu. The Hindu god of preservation. Vallalar sees him as an agent sustained and empowered by the one Grace-Light.
Yoga. Spiritual discipline or union. Vallalar frames the ultimate union and its resulting powers as gifts of divine grace.
